- Dithering on the FIVA Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool  (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved when hydraulic pressure is low. If this is the case the FIVA main spool is NOT Stuck.

FIVA Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->FIVA Feedback Supervision->FIVA Integrator Saturation
alarms.long_description: The FIVA controller integrator has compensated more than allowed.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on FIVA pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck FIVA pilot valve.
- FIVA Main Spool is stuck at tank or Injection position.
- FIVA pilot valve receives a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 always has an output more than 12 mA or always less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: FIVA Controller on CCU can no longer compensate completely for position errors. This will most likely affect mean pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Most likely the Parker Pilot valve is not calibrated precisely to compensate for zero overlap differences.

Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 FIVA Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check that the parker pilot Valve is not stuck or sticking
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved hydraulically.
- Testing the pilot valve and FIVA Valve can be checked using Engine stopped procedure, feeling dithering movement when pressure is above approx. 180 bar.


If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->ME-V Piston Supervision->MEV Piston Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ME-V timing piston not moving
alarms.cause:
- Cable Failure, or
- Sensor error, or
- ME-V timing piston stuck, or
- FIVA valve failure
alarms.effect:
- No exhaust valve timing control.
- Pcomp increases if piston is not moving
- Pmax may increase
- The limiter 'Compression pres.' is activated and it will not be possible to run the engine with
scavenge air pressure above the safe limit for running with ME-V failure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- ME-V piston feedback cabling
- FIVA valve 
- Pcomp and Pmax

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->EngineSide/Remote Control Selection->Inconsistent Control Stat. Request
alarms.long_description: The Control Station Switch Logic has detected inconsistent control signal requests. Cabling seem to be ok but values are inconsistent.
alarms.cause:
The control station switch logic expected a high/low combination of the control station request signals.

One of two events has occurred:
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both low.
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both high.
alarms.effect: The ECS retains its manoeuvre place.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check Ch23 CCU1 (Cable ID = 1118 for Local Control).
- Check Ch23 CCU2 (Cable ID = 1130 for Remote Control).
- Check Pressure Switches to see if sensors are  stuck High or Low. Replace faulty switch or cut out faulty sensor.
- If everything is OK: Replace CCU1 or CCU2.

alarms.suggested_action: - Check cabling, or\n- Check clutch sensor, or\n- If the signal is OK while the alarm is present, the MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid parameters

alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the MPC is not correct. The exact effect is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the MPC has just been replaced: Wait for automatic software download to complete.\nCheck MPC power supply and fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid software

alarms.cause: MPC is replaced while both MOP A and MOP B are unavailable.
alarms.effect: The ECS may be seriously affected if MPC is runs incorrect software. The exact behaviour is unknown since it also depends on which MPC is involved.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off MPC immediately. When either MOP A or MOP B is operating again, the MPC can be switched on again. When the automatic preparation of the MPC is finished the MPC will operate correctly again.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: The Parameter flash is corrupt.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If problem persist, the unit may be defect.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description:
At system in operation an ongoing ID-key test is made.
The alarm is set when a read byte in the ID-key is not equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
The alarm is reset as soon a read byte in the ID-key is equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
I. e. a problem also exists with the ID-key when the alarm are not set while it has not been acknowledged.
One byte is tested for each second. If the alarm does not reappear in a test cycle of 256 seconds, the fail on the ID-key is not steady.
alarms.cause: The ID-key is defect, is not plugged correct or is missing.
alarms.effect: No operational effect until the next restart.\nIf the ID-key is plugged correct, the persistent data is lost.
alarms.suggested_action: Ensure the ID-key is plugged correct in the system.\nIf plugged correctly and a system restart fails because of problems with the ID-key, replace the ID-key with a new.

alarms.synopsis: EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->EICU Commands->EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.long_description: CCU's receive commands from the EICU at regular intervals. The commands have been missing a number of times.
alarms.cause:
If all CCU's and ETU's report this alarm
- EICU Failure.

If alarm is released randomly from different CCU's and ETU's:
- Network failure.
alarms.effect:
- Engine remains operative. No load reduction required.
- Both ECR and RCS Control stations are no longer available. Only ESC can be used in this situation.
- Speedsetpoint will be 'locked in last' until ESC has been selected.
- Loss of remote control will be displayed on the RCS.
- Set point to and supervision of HPS is lost. The HPS will go to failsafe pressure level (if EIUC power is lost).
- Connection to alarm system is no longer available. Alarms are still displayed on MOP.
- Cylinder lubrication will be set to fail safe amount and lubrication will be speed proportional.
- Several values on the MOP display will be unavailable.
- HPS Slave pump is started (J80 = OFF) regardless of engine load, until the alarm condition is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCU's and ETU's permanently report this alarm: Check EICU:
- Check that the EICU is in normal mode (green LED on MPC)
- Replace EICU with new MPC.

If CCU's and ETU's randomly report this alarm:
- Check network status on MOP maintenance screen.
- Check for ground failure.
- Check all network cabling including terminating resistors.
- Check cable diagram for location of resistors.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value

alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level

alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable

- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Noise Detection Supervision->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the ECS system
alarms.cause:
- One or more ECS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or
- ECS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source

NOTE: 
Unless IRM module is used, the location of a ECS component causing the alarm is NOT limited to the MPC on which the alarm has appeared.
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the ECS system, e.g. 
- Exh. Valve Closed Position Changed
- Exh. Valve closing/opening too fast/slow (4 alarms)
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Total noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, MPCs for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Stop engine or reduce rpm to slow down level
If the MPC is equipped with IRM Module go to step 7
2. On one MPC: Disconnect power supply Connector J1
3. Observe if increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If the increase has stopped, the MPC with intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's
ground has been found  skip step 5 and continue to step 6
5. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1 in order for the MPC to resume normal function and go back to
step 2, choosing the next MPC
6. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1  the MPC will resume normal function.
7. Set the MPC in TEST MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the MPC's normal function.
8. Disconnect connections one at a time (from J2 to J85, - NOT J1), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
9. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
10.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
11.Set the MPC in NORNAL MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O

NOTE: 
If a CCU is disconnected or stopped for more than 20 minutes, establishing of emergency lubrication to the affected cylinder is recommended, by fitting of backup lubrication cables from EICU.

alarms.long_description: Channel input is out of range.
alarms.cause:

- Try to Invalidate the signal on the MPC that has raised the alarm. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Ch33,4102-B,ELFI/FIVA B Spool Posit->Suprv. Ch33,4102-B,ELFI/FIVA B Spoo
alarms.long_description: The signal from the sensor connected to the specified channel is out of range. The sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or
- Sensor failurer, or missing sensor power supply, or
- MPC input failure, or
- For On/Off type sensors the cause can be a missing or wrong supervision resistor (typically 6.8 kOhm).
alarms.effect: Valve control is stopped, causing no injections to the cylinder.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP Alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Check power supply to the sensor (measure voltage between A (negative) and D (positive)). If voltage is OK (18-32 Vdc): Replace sensor.
- Try to Invalidate the signal on the MPC that has raised the alarm. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

If the problem persists: The MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Tacho->Tacho set A->Tacho set A failure
alarms.long_description: Faulty or missing Tacho signals.
alarms.cause:
- Wiring, sensors or encoders are faulty, or
- Damaged tacho amplifier (loose connections in box, or.
- Loose connections in cable ends, or
- Damaged sensor support console, or
- Damaged teeth on tacho wheel (if fitted) , or
- Power failure (CCU1 powers Tacho Set A and CCU2 powers Tacho Set B).
alarms.effect:
The MPC had to change active set of tacho sensors. 
If both tacho sensor set A and B fail on one CCU:  
- Injection is stopped on one or two cylinders. 
- Cylinder lubrication is stopped on affected cylinders!
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCUs report tacho failure:
- Fault is most likely found in encoder/trigger ring sensors, amplifier or amplifier related cabling.
- If Tacho A reports the problem: Check flywheel sensor.

If only one CCU reports tacho failure:
- Check diode flash pattern (Ch40-Ch47) on MPC and compare to normally working CCU. This will verify CCU and cable connections.

If both Tacho Set A and B reports tacho failure:
- Backup lubrication cables MUST be mounted on affected cylinders.

If all signals on one tacho stay low:
- Check tacho sensor power. 
Hint: All sensor signals toggle between zero and high at least once per revolution.

To troubleshoot the problem: Perform tacho test on MOP:
- Navigate to Maintenance -> Function Test screen.
- Perform Tacho tests and follow instruction.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Inconsistent Stop Signals
alarms.long_description: The two redundant Stop signals used by the CCU do not have the same value.
alarms.cause: CCU Hard Wired and CCU from control network have transmitted inconsistent stop signals
alarms.effect:
Engine remains operative. No load reduction required.

Effects:
- Stop signals redundancy is lost.
alarms.suggested_action:
If Engine Running on Fuel:
- All stop sensors must measure a pressure less than 0.5 bar. This can be checked on the MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen Ch36 (Cable ID = 1101-x, where x=CCU Number).

If Engine Stopped (No Fuel):
- All stop sensors must measure a pressure above 4 bar. This can be checked on the MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen Ch36 (Cable ID = 1101-x, where x=CCU Number).

- Cut out faulty sensor.
- Replace faulty sensor  
- If pressure level is low near sensors: Check pipes and fittings for leaks

Notice redundant stop sensor arrangement:
 CCU1, CCU3, CCU5: Redundant STOP from CCU2 Ch36
 CCU2, CCU4, CCU6: Redundant STOP from CCU1 Ch36

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Cylinder Lubrication->Alpha Lubricator A->Failing Lubr. FeedBack (Slowdown)

alarms.cause:

- Activation signal to solinoide missing, or
- Internal lubricator failure, or
- Feedback sensor not working, or
- Hydraulic pressure lost. Valve(s) 560 are closed.
alarms.effect: - Slowdown request is send from ECS.\n- No cylinder lubrication on the affected cylinder.\n- ECS will keep attempting to activate the injector electrically.
alarms.suggested_action:
LED in lubricator solinoide plug flashes:
- Check that valve(s) 560 are open.
- Replace lubricator with a spare.

If the problem persists:
- Check cable between lubricator and MPC.
- If cable path OK: Replace MPC.

LED in lubricator solinoide plug don't flash:
- Check cable path from MPC to solinoide plug.
- If cable path OK: Replace MPC

alarms.suggested_action:

- Check that heat tracer is on.
- Disassemble pipes and check if cylinder oil still flows.

- Replace lubricator level switch.

alarms.synopsis: Cyl. A Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Speed Controller->Cyl. A Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.long_description: The Governor is calculating a Fuel Index based on a backup telegram. This will occur in case of CCU failure.
alarms.cause: The CCU which should send the primary telegram is not on the control network or has stopped running, or \nControl Network problems caused prolonged transfer times.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but Mean Indicated Pressure may drift on affected cylinder.
alarms.suggested_action:

- Check that all CCUs are running and on the control network. Look for related alarms on MOP.

If the alarm persists during normal running note Engine RPM and direction and contact MAN Diesel when convenient

alarms.long_description: The hydraulic supply pressure has dropped. To compensate for insufficient pump flow maximum allowed fuel index is reduced. Fuel index reduction leads to lower hydraulic oil consumption.
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic supply Pump failure, or\n- Hydraulic leakage or failing bypass valves in the hydraulic supply system, or\n- One or more hydraulic supply pumps stopped.
alarms.effect: Engine load might be reduced and engine might run with unstable speed and fuel index. \n\n- If the pressure drops below a predefined level fuel injection is stopped.
alarms.suggested_action:
While locating the failure that causes the pressure drop: Reduce engine load to avoid unstable running. 

- Check for hydraulic pump related alarms. 
- Check for hydraulic leakages, pressure relief valve and failing bypass valves. Typically a failing bypass valve increases significantly in temperature.

Engine Stopped:
- Cut out individual HCU's to determine the location of the  leakage.
- Check the hydraulic pressure decay times on Auxiliaries -> Hydraulic System screen. Compare to reference.

alarms.synopsis: STOP Low While Engine Not Running
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->STOP Low While Engine Not Running
alarms.long_description: Pneumatic STOP signals are off while the engine is stopped. \nSTOP signals are measured by one pressure sensor on each CCU.\nThe pressure sensors are activated by control air supply and connected to CCUs Channel 36.
alarms.cause: - Loss of control air pressure, or\n- Engine stopped unexpectedly.
alarms.effect: If a start attempt is made while this alarm is present air and fuel may be applied simultaneously. This might damage the starting air bursting cap. Avoid Engine start.
alarms.suggested_action:
On the Maintenance -> System View I/O screen: Compare pressure measurements on all CCUs (channel 36). 
STOP is on when pressure is above approximately 2 bar. 

If only one CCU reports this failure:
- Check for pipe leakages near pressure sensor. 
- Check pressure sensor.

If all CCUs reports this failure:
- Check control air supply pressure according to instruction manual. 
- Check double non return valve at engine side. This valve is located in Engine Side Console.
- Check for leakages in the control air system.

If engine stopped unexpectedly: Move handle to stop position to clear the alarm.

alarms.synopsis: Max. Time in Pos. Table Reached
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Fuel Injection->Injection Profile 1->Max. Time in Pos. Table Reached
alarms.long_description: Fuel index ordered has resulted in an ELFI close time that is not supported for the current injection profile.
alarms.cause: - Engine running excessively heavy.\n- Fuel quality is poor\n- Profile shaping causing very long delays.
alarms.effect: Maximum time in position table for current injection profile is used. This means that regardless of how much Fuel index is increased Fuel amount into cylinders does not increase.
alarms.suggested_action:
Contact MAN B&W for the following adjustments:
- Increase maximum time in position table
- Injection Profile is too 'weak'. Make injection profile more aggressive.
- Freeze times are too long resulting in large close times.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Exhaust Valve Timing->MEV Activation Adaption->Return delay out of range
alarms.long_description: Measured ME-V return delay out of range. ME-V piston movement is too fast or too slow.
alarms.cause:
- Failing ELFI/FIVA Valve
-Failing piston feedback sensor,
- Too high friction in ME-V timing unit (too slow),
- Leakages in timing unit (too fast)
alarms.effect: ECS not able to control exhaust valve timing. Deviation on cylinder compression pressure may be present. Risk of too high compression and maximum pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce Engine load to reduce compression and maximum pressure.

Adjust actual compression and maximum pressure on MOP.

Check:
- ELFI/FIVA alarms
- ME-V Piston feedback sensor
- For leakages at timing unit.

Use HCU Events on MOP to compare ME-V piston feedback signal to other units.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->ELFI Valve A->ELFIA Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: The position feedback on the specific injection controlling valve has shown movements that are not physically realistic.
alarms.cause: Typically loose connection in cabling. Malfunction of internal ELFI-feedback electronics can cause out of range feedback signals.
alarms.effect: When the fault is detected injections are stopped until valve is reactivated via the Engine -> Chief Limiters MOP screen.\n\nThis alarm is a trigger member for the HCU Events screen (Maintaince->TroubleShooting). A log of the incident has been recorded and can be used to further analyse the alarm.
alarms.suggested_action:
Fuel injection is reactivated by toggling invalidation of CCU channel 30 (Maintenance -> System View I/O screen), re-enabling fuel injection on the Engine -> Chief Limiters screen, or CCU power off/on. Before doing any of the above check the following due to danger of Cover Lift:
- Check that Maintenance -> System View I/O -> CCUx-Ch30 -> Electrical Value never is out of range (3.5-20.5 mA)
- Inspect entire cabling from CCU to ELFI Valve.
- If cabling is OK and reactivation does not solve the problem: Replace CCU, 
- If CCU replacement does not solve the problem: Replace ELFI Valve and reactivate as described.

During reactivation: Try to feel the dither on the valve (pressure must be sufficiently high, above approx. 180 bar.

alarms.synopsis: ELFIA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->ELFIA Feedback Supervision->ELFIA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.long_description: ELFI main spool is at Tank position when it should not be.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on ELFI pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck ELFI pilot valve.
- ELFI Main Spool is stuck at tank position.
- ELFI pilot valve receives a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 (ELFIA) or Ch71 (ELFIB) always has an output less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: Injection will not occur as long as this situation is present. However injection will automatically start again when cause of alarm is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 ELFI Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check if the ELFI main spool can be moved hydraulically 
- Dithering on the ELFI Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move ELFI Main Spool (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).

ELFI Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move ELFI Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- ELFI Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
- ELFI Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- ELFI Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.long_description: The ELFI controller integrator has compensated more than allowed.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on ELFI pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck ELFI pilot valve.
- ELFI Main Spool is stuck at tank or Injection position.
- ELFI pilot valve recieves a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 (ELFIA) or Ch71 (ELFIB) always has an output more than 12 mA or always less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: ELFI Controller on CCU can no longer compensate completely for position errors. This will most likely affect mean pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Most likely the Parker Pilot valve is not calibrated precisely to compensate for zero overlap differences.

Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).

- Check that the parker pilot Valve is not stuck or sticking
- Check if the ELFI main spool can be moved hydraulically.
- Testing the pilot valve and ELFI Valve can be checked using Engine stopped procedure, feeling dithering movement when pressure is above approx. 180 bar.

- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 FIVA Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved hydraulically 
- Dithering on the FIVA Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).

FIVA Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
-FIVA Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.synopsis: FIVA Fault:Main Spool at Inj. Pos.
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->FIVA Feedback Supervision->FIVA Fault:Main Spool at Inj. Pos.
alarms.long_description: FIVA main spool is at Injection position when it should not be.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Mechanically stuck FIVA pilot valve.
- FIVA Main Spool is stuck at Injection position.
- CCU Ch70 always has an output more than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: Injection will not occur as long as this situation is present. However injection will automatically start again when cause of alarm is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 FIVA Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Dithering on the FIVA Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool  (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved when hydraulic pressure is low. If this is the case the FIVA main spool is NOT Stuck.

FIVA Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->FIVA Feedback Supervision->FIVA Integrator Saturation
alarms.long_description: The FIVA controller integrator has compensated more than allowed.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on FIVA pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck FIVA pilot valve.
- FIVA Main Spool is stuck at tank or Injection position.
- FIVA pilot valve receives a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 always has an output more than 12 mA or always less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: FIVA Controller on CCU can no longer compensate completely for position errors. This will most likely affect mean pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Most likely the Parker Pilot valve is not calibrated precisely to compensate for zero overlap differences.

Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 FIVA Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check that the parker pilot Valve is not stuck or sticking
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved hydraulically.
- Testing the pilot valve and FIVA Valve can be checked using Engine stopped procedure, feeling dithering movement when pressure is above approx. 180 bar.


If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->ME-V Piston Supervision->MEV Piston Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ME-V timing piston not moving
alarms.cause:
- Cable Failure, or
- Sensor error, or
- ME-V timing piston stuck, or
- FIVA valve failure
alarms.effect:
- No exhaust valve timing control.
- Pcomp increases if piston is not moving
- Pmax may increase
- The limiter 'Compression pres.' is activated and it will not be possible to run the engine with
scavenge air pressure above the safe limit for running with ME-V failure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- ME-V piston feedback cabling
- FIVA valve 
- Pcomp and Pmax

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->EngineSide/Remote Control Selection->Inconsistent Control Stat. Request
alarms.long_description: The Control Station Switch Logic has detected inconsistent control signal requests. Cabling seem to be ok but values are inconsistent.
alarms.cause:
The control station switch logic expected a high/low combination of the control station request signals.

One of two events has occurred:
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both low.
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both high.
alarms.effect: The ECS retains its manoeuvre place.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check Ch23 CCU1 (Cable ID = 1118 for Local Control).
- Check Ch23 CCU2 (Cable ID = 1130 for Remote Control).
- Check Pressure Switches to see if sensors are  stuck High or Low. Replace faulty switch or cut out faulty sensor.
- If everything is OK: Replace CCU1 or CCU2.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Generator clutch signals deviate
alarms.long_description: Redundant generator clutch state signals deviate.
alarms.cause: - Cabling failure, or\n- Clutch sensor failure, or\n- MPC input failure
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check cabling, or\n- Check clutch sensor, or\n- If the signal is OK while the alarm is present, the MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Dual tacho signals not valid
alarms.long_description: Speed measured on tacho C/D is not valid.
alarms.cause: - Tacho C/ D encoder failure, or \n- Speed measured by tacho C/D deviates too much from speed measured by tacho A/B.
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check tacho C/D sensors, or\n- Check tacho C/D cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.long_description: The watchdog on the MPC has been disabled.
alarms.cause: Wrong setting of the orange DIP-switch on the MPC.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but with watchdogs disabled the MPC may not respond correctly to software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: Check that MPC DIP-switch is enabled (orange switch must be ON).

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Non standard baud rate
alarms.long_description: Baud rate for service terminal is not 9600 Bd.
alarms.cause: Non-standard Baud rate selected
alarms.effect: No, or unreadable output to service terminal.
alarms.suggested_action: Reset blue DIP, and reboot MPC when appropriate.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: Invalid MPC parameters. The MPC cannot start with incorrect parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm appears when the MPC automatically loads the wrong parameter set after MPC replacement.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the MPC is not correct. The exact effect is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the MPC has just been replaced: Wait for automatic software download to complete.\nCheck MPC power supply and fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: The MPC is running an incorrect application program
alarms.cause: MPC is replaced while both MOP A and MOP B are unavailable.
alarms.effect: The ECS may be seriously affected if MPC is runs incorrect software. The exact behaviour is unknown since it also depends on which MPC is involved.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off MPC immediately. When either MOP A or MOP B is operating again, the MPC can be switched on again. When the automatic preparation of the MPC is finished the MPC will operate correctly again.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: The Parameter flash is corrupt.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If problem persist, the unit may be defect.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description:
At system in operation an ongoing ID-key test is made.
The alarm is set when a read byte in the ID-key is not equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
The alarm is reset as soon a read byte in the ID-key is equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
I. e. a problem also exists with the ID-key when the alarm are not set while it has not been acknowledged.
One byte is tested for each second. If the alarm does not reappear in a test cycle of 256 seconds, the fail on the ID-key is not steady.
alarms.cause: The ID-key is defect, is not plugged correct or is missing.
alarms.effect: No operational effect until the next restart.\nIf the ID-key is plugged correct, the persistent data is lost.
alarms.suggested_action: Ensure the ID-key is plugged correct in the system.\nIf plugged correctly and a system restart fails because of problems with the ID-key, replace the ID-key with a new.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power B failure, connector 1C

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power A failure, connector 1B

alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply A for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply A is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.

alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F12 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 12 is blown. Fuse 12 protects the sensor power supply, terminal 'D', of the analogue inputs, channels 20 to 37, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the sensors and signals connected to channels 20 to 37 may give wrong values, and a number of supervision alarms may occur simultaneously.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 20 to 37. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F13 failure

Fuse 13 is blown. Fuse 13 protects the power outlets of:
channels 40 to 47, terminal 'D', 
channels 48 to 53, terminal 'E',
channels 60 and 61, terminal 'H'.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the signals related to channels 40 to 61 may be wrong. Effect on engine behaviour is unknown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for possible failures in the external cabling to channels 40 to 61. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F14 failure

alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: Injections will not occur on cylinders controlled by this MPC.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F9 failure

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Battery Level Low
alarms.long_description: MPC battery level low.
alarms.cause: Battery discharged.
alarms.effect: If MPC remains switched on, there is no effect. If the MPC is switched off or power is lost, the MPC will loose its time settings. Time settings will be automatically retrieved at next power on.
alarms.suggested_action:
At next engine stop:
 1) Remove power supply on MPC.
 2) Replace battery.
 3) Reconnect power supply.

alarms.synopsis: EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->EICU Commands->EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.long_description: CCU's receive commands from the EICU at regular intervals. The commands have been missing a number of times.
alarms.cause:
If all CCU's and ETU's report this alarm
- EICU Failure.

If alarm is released randomly from different CCU's and ETU's:
- Network failure.
alarms.effect:
- Engine remains operative. No load reduction required.
- Both ECR and RCS Control stations are no longer available. Only ESC can be used in this situation.
- Speedsetpoint will be 'locked in last' until ESC has been selected.
- Loss of remote control will be displayed on the RCS.
- Set point to and supervision of HPS is lost. The HPS will go to failsafe pressure level (if EIUC power is lost).
- Connection to alarm system is no longer available. Alarms are still displayed on MOP.
- Cylinder lubrication will be set to fail safe amount and lubrication will be speed proportional.
- Several values on the MOP display will be unavailable.
- HPS Slave pump is started (J80 = OFF) regardless of engine load, until the alarm condition is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCU's and ETU's permanently report this alarm: Check EICU:
- Check that the EICU is in normal mode (green LED on MPC)
- Replace EICU with new MPC.

If CCU's and ETU's randomly report this alarm:
- Check network status on MOP maintenance screen.
- Check for ground failure.
- Check all network cabling including terminating resistors.
- Check cable diagram for location of resistors.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Noise Detection Supervision->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the ECS system
alarms.cause:
- One or more ECS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or
- ECS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source

NOTE: 
Unless IRM module is used, the location of a ECS component causing the alarm is NOT limited to the MPC on which the alarm has appeared.
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the ECS system, e.g. 
- Exh. Valve Closed Position Changed
- Exh. Valve closing/opening too fast/slow (4 alarms)
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Total noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, MPCs for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Stop engine or reduce rpm to slow down level
If the MPC is equipped with IRM Module go to step 7
2. On one MPC: Disconnect power supply Connector J1
3. Observe if increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If the increase has stopped, the MPC with intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's
ground has been found  skip step 5 and continue to step 6
5. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1 in order for the MPC to resume normal function and go back to
step 2, choosing the next MPC
6. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1  the MPC will resume normal function.
7. Set the MPC in TEST MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the MPC's normal function.
8. Disconnect connections one at a time (from J2 to J85, - NOT J1), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
9. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
10.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
11.Set the MPC in NORNAL MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O

NOTE: 
If a CCU is disconnected or stopped for more than 20 minutes, establishing of emergency lubrication to the affected cylinder is recommended, by fitting of backup lubrication cables from EICU.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Ch20,2150,Engine Side Speed Set->Suprv. Ch20,2150,Engine Side Speed
alarms.long_description: Invalid input, so MPC uses the last valid value.
alarms.cause: Channel input is out of range.
alarms.effect: The input value is fixed to last valid input and ESC is not possible.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check ESC speed handle cable to CCU1 (Ch20).\n- If active control station is ESC: Change control station.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Ch20,2156,Engine Side Speed Increas->Suprv. Ch20,2156,Engine Side Speed
alarms.long_description: Channel input is out of range.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or
- Sensor failurer, or missing sensor power supply, or
- MPC input failure, or
- For On/Off type sensors the cause can be a missing or wrong supervision resistor (typically 6.8 kOhm).
alarms.effect: The input value is fixed to last valid input and ESC is not possible.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP Alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Check power supply to the sensor (measure voltage between A (negative) and D (positive)). If voltage is OK (18-32 Vdc): Replace sensor.
- Try to Invalidate the signal on the MPC that has raised the alarm. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

If the problem persists: The MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Ch24,8601,Scavenge Air Pressure->Suprv. Ch24,8601,Scavenge Air Press

alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or

- MPC input failure, or

alarms.effect:
Scavenge air pressure signal is no longer available.
- Fuel injection timing is now based on a predefined angle.
- Compression pressure limiter is no longer active. 
- No safeguard against, high compression pressure.
- To high compression pressure can cause cylinder cover lift.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor
- MPC Input

- Use PMI equipment to verify compression and maximum pressure

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Tacho->Tacho set A->Tacho set A failure
alarms.long_description: Faulty or missing Tacho signals.
alarms.cause:
- Wiring, sensors or encoders are faulty, or
- Damaged tacho amplifier (loose connections in box, or.
- Loose connections in cable ends, or
- Damaged sensor support console, or
- Damaged teeth on tacho wheel (if fitted) , or
- Power failure (CCU1 powers Tacho Set A and CCU2 powers Tacho Set B).
alarms.effect:
The MPC had to change active set of tacho sensors. 
If both tacho sensor set A and B fail on one CCU:  
- Injection is stopped on one or two cylinders. 
- Cylinder lubrication is stopped on affected cylinders!
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCUs report tacho failure:
- Fault is most likely found in encoder/trigger ring sensors, amplifier or amplifier related cabling.
- If Tacho A reports the problem: Check flywheel sensor.

If only one CCU reports tacho failure:
- Check diode flash pattern (Ch40-Ch47) on MPC and compare to normally working CCU. This will verify CCU and cable connections.

If both Tacho Set A and B reports tacho failure:
- Backup lubrication cables MUST be mounted on affected cylinders.

If all signals on one tacho stay low:
- Check tacho sensor power. 
Hint: All sensor signals toggle between zero and high at least once per revolution.

To troubleshoot the problem: Perform tacho test on MOP:
- Navigate to Maintenance -> Function Test screen.
- Perform Tacho tests and follow instruction.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Tacho->Delta Tacho B too big

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Inconsistent Stop Signals
alarms.long_description: The two redundant Stop signals used by the CCU do not have the same value.
alarms.cause: CCU Hard Wired and CCU from control network have transmitted inconsistent stop signals
alarms.effect:
Engine remains operative. No load reduction required.

Effects:
- Stop signals redundancy is lost.
alarms.suggested_action:
If Engine Running on Fuel:
- All stop sensors must measure a pressure less than 0.5 bar. This can be checked on the MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen Ch36 (Cable ID = 1101-x, where x=CCU Number).

If Engine Stopped (No Fuel):
- All stop sensors must measure a pressure above 4 bar. This can be checked on the MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen Ch36 (Cable ID = 1101-x, where x=CCU Number).

- Cut out faulty sensor.
- Replace faulty sensor  
- If pressure level is low near sensors: Check pipes and fittings for leaks

Notice redundant stop sensor arrangement:
 CCU1, CCU3, CCU5: Redundant STOP from CCU2 Ch36
 CCU2, CCU4, CCU6: Redundant STOP from CCU1 Ch36

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Cylinder Lubrication->Alpha Lubricator A->Failing Lubr. FeedBack (Slowdown)

- Activation signal to solinoide missing, or
- Internal lubricator failure, or
- Feedback sensor not working, or
- Hydraulic pressure lost. Valve(s) 560 are closed.
alarms.effect: - Slowdown request is send from ECS.\n- No cylinder lubrication on the affected cylinder.\n- ECS will keep attempting to activate the injector electrically.
alarms.suggested_action:
LED in lubricator solinoide plug flashes:
- Check that valve(s) 560 are open.
- Replace lubricator with a spare.

If the problem persists:
- Check cable between lubricator and MPC.
- If cable path OK: Replace MPC.

LED in lubricator solinoide plug don't flash:
- Check cable path from MPC to solinoide plug.
- If cable path OK: Replace MPC

alarms.synopsis: Cyl. A Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Speed Controller->Cyl. A Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.long_description: The Governor is calculating a Fuel Index based on a backup telegram. This will occur in case of CCU failure.
alarms.cause: The CCU which should send the primary telegram is not on the control network or has stopped running, or \nControl Network problems caused prolonged transfer times.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but Mean Indicated Pressure may drift on affected cylinder.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Measure Mean Indicated Pressure using a PMI system to ensure that the cylinders are balanced. If necessary, adjust mean indicated pressure on MOP.
- Check that all CCUs are running and on the control network. Look for related alarms on MOP.

If the alarm persists during normal running note Engine RPM and direction and contact MAN Diesel when convenient

alarms.synopsis: Cyl. B Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Speed Controller->Cyl. B Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.long_description: The Governor is calculating a Fuel Index based on a backup telegram. This will occur in case of CCU failure.
alarms.cause: The CCU which should send the primary telegram is not on the control network or has stopped running, or \nControl Network problems caused prolonged transfer times.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but Mean Indicated Pressure may drift on affected cylinder.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Measure Mean Indicated Pressure using a PMI system to ensure that the cylinders are balanced. If necessary, adjust mean indicated pressure on MOP.
- Check that all CCUs are running and on the control network. Look for related alarms on MOP.

If the alarm persists during normal running note Engine RPM and direction and contact MAN Diesel when convenient

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Fuel Index Limiters->Torque Limiter->Dynamic Torque Limiter->Dynamic Torque Limiter Time Out
alarms.long_description: Dynamic torque limiter time out
alarms.cause: This alarm indicates that the engine have used the dynamic torque limiter for as long time as allowed
alarms.effect: The torque limiter will decrease to the limiter level allowed for continous operation
alarms.suggested_action: Pressing 'Increase limits' will disregard the time limitations and increase the limiter level to the same level as normally allowed by the dynamic torque limiter. This is not recommend for continuous operation

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Fuel Index Limiters->Hydraulic Supply Pressure Limiter->Low Hydraulic Pressure
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic supply pressure has dropped. To compensate for insufficient pump flow maximum allowed fuel index is reduced. Fuel index reduction leads to lower hydraulic oil consumption.
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic supply Pump failure, or\n- Hydraulic leakage or failing bypass valves in the hydraulic supply system, or\n- One or more hydraulic supply pumps stopped.
alarms.effect: Engine load might be reduced and engine might run with unstable speed and fuel index. \n\n- If the pressure drops below a predefined level fuel injection is stopped.
alarms.suggested_action:
While locating the failure that causes the pressure drop: Reduce engine load to avoid unstable running. 

- Check for hydraulic pump related alarms. 
- Check for hydraulic leakages, pressure relief valve and failing bypass valves. Typically a failing bypass valve increases significantly in temperature.

Engine Stopped:
- Cut out individual HCU's to determine the location of the  leakage.
- Check the hydraulic pressure decay times on Auxiliaries -> Hydraulic System screen. Compare to reference.

alarms.synopsis: STOP Low While Engine Not Running
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->STOP Low While Engine Not Running
alarms.long_description: Pneumatic STOP signals are off while the engine is stopped. \nSTOP signals are measured by one pressure sensor on each CCU.\nThe pressure sensors are activated by control air supply and connected to CCUs Channel 36.
alarms.cause: - Loss of control air pressure, or\n- Engine stopped unexpectedly.
alarms.effect: If a start attempt is made while this alarm is present air and fuel may be applied simultaneously. This might damage the starting air bursting cap. Avoid Engine start.
alarms.suggested_action:
On the Maintenance -> System View I/O screen: Compare pressure measurements on all CCUs (channel 36). 
STOP is on when pressure is above approximately 2 bar. 

If only one CCU reports this failure:
- Check for pipe leakages near pressure sensor. 
- Check pressure sensor.

If all CCUs reports this failure:
- Check control air supply pressure according to instruction manual. 
- Check double non return valve at engine side. This valve is located in Engine Side Console.
- Check for leakages in the control air system.

If engine stopped unexpectedly: Move handle to stop position to clear the alarm.

alarms.synopsis: Max. Time in Pos. Table Reached
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Fuel Injection->Injection Profile 1->Max. Time in Pos. Table Reached
alarms.long_description: Fuel index ordered has resulted in an ELFI close time that is not supported for the current injection profile.
alarms.cause: - Engine running excessively heavy.\n- Fuel quality is poor\n- Profile shaping causing very long delays.
alarms.effect: Maximum time in position table for current injection profile is used. This means that regardless of how much Fuel index is increased Fuel amount into cylinders does not increase.
alarms.suggested_action:
Contact MAN B&W for the following adjustments:
- Increase maximum time in position table
- Injection Profile is too 'weak'. Make injection profile more aggressive.
- Freeze times are too long resulting in large close times.

alarms.cause:
- Failing ELFI/FIVA Valve
-Failing piston feedback sensor,
- Too high friction in ME-V timing unit (too slow),

alarms.effect: When the fault is detected injections are stopped until valve is reactivated via the Engine -> Chief Limiters MOP screen.\n\nThis alarm is a trigger member for the HCU Events screen (Maintaince->TroubleShooting). A log of the incident has been recorded and can be used to further analyse the alarm.
alarms.suggested_action:
Fuel injection is reactivated by toggling invalidation of CCU channel 30 (Maintenance -> System View I/O screen), re-enabling fuel injection on the Engine -> Chief Limiters screen, or CCU power off/on. Before doing any of the above check the following due to danger of Cover Lift:
- Check that Maintenance -> System View I/O -> CCUx-Ch30 -> Electrical Value never is out of range (3.5-20.5 mA)
- Inspect entire cabling from CCU to ELFI Valve.
- If cabling is OK and reactivation does not solve the problem: Replace CCU, 
- If CCU replacement does not solve the problem: Replace ELFI Valve and reactivate as described.

During reactivation: Try to feel the dither on the valve (pressure must be sufficiently high, above approx. 180 bar.

alarms.synopsis: ELFIA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->ELFIA Feedback Supervision->ELFIA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.long_description: ELFI main spool is at Tank position when it should not be.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on ELFI pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck ELFI pilot valve.
- ELFI Main Spool is stuck at tank position.
- ELFI pilot valve receives a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 (ELFIA) or Ch71 (ELFIB) always has an output less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: Injection will not occur as long as this situation is present. However injection will automatically start again when cause of alarm is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 ELFI Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check if the ELFI main spool can be moved hydraulically 
- Dithering on the ELFI Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move ELFI Main Spool (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).

ELFI Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move ELFI Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- ELFI Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
- ELFI Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- ELFI Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.suggested_action:

- CCU Ch70 (ELFIA) or Ch71 (ELFIB) always has an output more than 12 mA or always less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: ELFI Controller on CCU can no longer compensate completely for position errors. This will most likely affect mean pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Most likely the Parker Pilot valve is not calibrated precisely enough to compensate for zero overlap differences or wear in service..

Check the following:
- Ch 71 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-B).
- Ch33 ELFI Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check that the parker pilot Valve is not stuck or sticking.
- Check if the ELFI main spool can be moved hydraulically.
- Testing the pilot valve and ELFI Valve can be checked using Engine stopped procedure, feeling dithering movement when pressure is above approx. 180 bar.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- ELFI Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.synopsis: FIVA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->FIVA Feedback Supervision->FIVA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.long_description: FIVA main spool is at Tank position when it should not be.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on FIVA pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck FIVA pilot valve.
- FIVA Main Spool is stuck at tank position.
- FIVA pilot valve receives a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 always has an output less than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: Injection will not occur as long as this situation is present. However injection will automatically start again when cause of alarm is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 FIVA Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved hydraulically 
- Dithering on the FIVA Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).

FIVA Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
-FIVA Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.synopsis: FIVA Fault:Main Spool at Inj. Pos.
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->FIVA Feedback Supervision->FIVA Fault:Main Spool at Inj. Pos.
alarms.long_description: FIVA main spool is at Injection position when it should not be.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Mechanically stuck FIVA pilot valve.
- FIVA Main Spool is stuck at Injection position.
- CCU Ch70 always has an output more than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: Injection will not occur as long as this situation is present. However injection will automatically start again when cause of alarm is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 FIVA Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Dithering on the FIVA Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool  (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved when hydraulic pressure is low. If this is the case the FIVA main spool is NOT Stuck.

FIVA Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move FIVA Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
- FIVA Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.effect: FIVA Controller on CCU can no longer compensate completely for position errors. This will most likely affect mean pressure.

Most likely the Parker Pilot valve is not calibrated precisely to compensate for zero overlap differences.

Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 FIVA Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check that the parker pilot Valve is not stuck or sticking
- Check if the FIVA main spool can be moved hydraulically.
- Testing the pilot valve and FIVA Valve can be checked using Engine stopped procedure, feeling dithering movement when pressure is above approx. 180 bar.


If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:

- CCU reporting the problem.
- FIVA Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->ME-V Piston Supervision->MEV Piston Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ME-V timing piston not moving
alarms.cause:
- Cable Failure, or

- ME-V timing piston stuck, or

alarms.effect:
- No exhaust valve timing control.
- Pcomp increases if piston is not moving
- Pmax may increase
- The limiter 'Compression pres.' is activated and it will not be possible to run the engine with
scavenge air pressure above the safe limit for running with ME-V failure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:

- FIVA valve 
- Pcomp and Pmax

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->EngineSide/Remote Control Selection->Inconsistent Control Stat. Request
alarms.long_description: The Control Station Switch Logic has detected inconsistent control signal requests. Cabling seem to be ok but values are inconsistent.
alarms.cause:
The control station switch logic expected a high/low combination of the control station request signals.

One of two events has occurred:
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both low.
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both high.
alarms.effect: The ECS retains its manoeuvre place.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check Ch23 CCU1 (Cable ID = 1118 for Local Control).
- Check Ch23 CCU2 (Cable ID = 1130 for Remote Control).
- Check Pressure Switches to see if sensors are  stuck High or Low. Replace faulty switch or cut out faulty sensor.
- If everything is OK: Replace CCU1 or CCU2.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Generator clutch signals deviate
alarms.long_description: Redundant generator clutch state signals deviate.
alarms.cause: - Cabling failure, or\n- Clutch sensor failure, or\n- MPC input failure
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check cabling, or\n- Check clutch sensor, or\n- If the signal is OK while the alarm is present, the MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Dual tacho signals not valid
alarms.long_description: Speed measured on tacho C/D is not valid.
alarms.cause: - Tacho C/ D encoder failure, or \n- Speed measured by tacho C/D deviates too much from speed measured by tacho A/B.
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check tacho C/D sensors, or\n- Check tacho C/D cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.long_description: The watchdog on the MPC has been disabled.
alarms.cause: Wrong setting of the orange DIP-switch on the MPC.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but with watchdogs disabled the MPC may not respond correctly to software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: Check that MPC DIP-switch is enabled (orange switch must be ON).

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Non standard baud rate
alarms.long_description: Baud rate for service terminal is not 9600 Bd.
alarms.cause: Non-standard Baud rate selected
alarms.effect: No, or unreadable output to service terminal.
alarms.suggested_action: Reset blue DIP, and reboot MPC when appropriate.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: Invalid MPC parameters. The MPC cannot start with incorrect parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm appears when the MPC automatically loads the wrong parameter set after MPC replacement.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the MPC is not correct. The exact effect is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the MPC has just been replaced: Wait for automatic software download to complete.\nCheck MPC power supply and fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: The MPC is running an incorrect application program
alarms.cause: MPC is replaced while both MOP A and MOP B are unavailable.
alarms.effect: The ECS may be seriously affected if MPC is runs incorrect software. The exact behaviour is unknown since it also depends on which MPC is involved.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off MPC immediately. When either MOP A or MOP B is operating again, the MPC can be switched on again. When the automatic preparation of the MPC is finished the MPC will operate correctly again.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: The Parameter flash is corrupt.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If problem persist, the unit may be defect.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description:
At system in operation an ongoing ID-key test is made.
The alarm is set when a read byte in the ID-key is not equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
The alarm is reset as soon a read byte in the ID-key is equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
I. e. a problem also exists with the ID-key when the alarm are not set while it has not been acknowledged.
One byte is tested for each second. If the alarm does not reappear in a test cycle of 256 seconds, the fail on the ID-key is not steady.
alarms.cause: The ID-key is defect, is not plugged correct or is missing.
alarms.effect: No operational effect until the next restart.\nIf the ID-key is plugged correct, the persistent data is lost.
alarms.suggested_action: Ensure the ID-key is plugged correct in the system.\nIf plugged correctly and a system restart fails because of problems with the ID-key, replace the ID-key with a new.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power B failure, connector 1C
alarms.long_description: No power on theMPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal C.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply B for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply B is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply A.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power A failure, connector 1B
alarms.long_description: No power on the MPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal B.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply A for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply A is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply B.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F12 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 12 is blown. Fuse 12 protects the sensor power supply, terminal 'D', of the analogue inputs, channels 20 to 37, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the sensors and signals connected to channels 20 to 37 may give wrong values, and a number of supervision alarms may occur simultaneously.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 20 to 37. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F13 failure
alarms.long_description:
Fuse 13 is blown. Fuse 13 protects the power outlets of:
channels 40 to 47, terminal 'D', 
channels 48 to 53, terminal 'E',
channels 60 and 61, terminal 'H'.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the signals related to channels 40 to 61 may be wrong. Effect on engine behaviour is unknown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for possible failures in the external cabling to channels 40 to 61. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F14 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 14 is blown. Fuse 14 protects the power supply for the analog output, channels 70 and 71, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: Injections will not occur on cylinders controlled by this MPC.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 70 and 71. Replace the fuse. If the fuse blows again: Replaced the MPC.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F9 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 9 is blown. Fuse 9 protects power supply connector 9 of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.

alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to connector 9. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Battery Level Low
alarms.long_description: MPC battery level low.
alarms.cause: Battery discharged.
alarms.effect: If MPC remains switched on, there is no effect. If the MPC is switched off or power is lost, the MPC will loose its time settings. Time settings will be automatically retrieved at next power on.
alarms.suggested_action:
At next engine stop:
 1) Remove power supply on MPC.
 2) Replace battery.
 3) Reconnect power supply.

alarms.synopsis: EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->EICU Commands->EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.long_description: CCU's receive commands from the EICU at regular intervals. The commands have been missing a number of times.
alarms.cause:
If all CCU's and ETU's report this alarm
- EICU Failure.

If alarm is released randomly from different CCU's and ETU's:
- Network failure.
alarms.effect:
- Engine remains operative. No load reduction required.
- Both ECR and RCS Control stations are no longer available. Only ESC can be used in this situation.
- Speedsetpoint will be 'locked in last' until ESC has been selected.
- Loss of remote control will be displayed on the RCS.
- Set point to and supervision of HPS is lost. The HPS will go to failsafe pressure level (if EIUC power is lost).
- Connection to alarm system is no longer available. Alarms are still displayed on MOP.
- Cylinder lubrication will be set to fail safe amount and lubrication will be speed proportional.
- Several values on the MOP display will be unavailable.
- HPS Slave pump is started (J80 = OFF) regardless of engine load, until the alarm condition is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCU's and ETU's permanently report this alarm: Check EICU:
- Check that the EICU is in normal mode (green LED on MPC)
- Replace EICU with new MPC.

If CCU's and ETU's randomly report this alarm:
- Check network status on MOP maintenance screen.
- Check for ground failure.
- Check all network cabling including terminating resistors.
- Check cable diagram for location of resistors.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Noise Detection Supervision->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the ECS system
alarms.cause:
- One or more ECS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or
- ECS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source

NOTE: 
Unless IRM module is used, the location of a ECS component causing the alarm is NOT limited to the MPC on which the alarm has appeared.
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the ECS system, e.g. 
- Exh. Valve Closed Position Changed
- Exh. Valve closing/opening too fast/slow (4 alarms)
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Total noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, MPCs for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Stop engine or reduce rpm to slow down level
If the MPC is equipped with IRM Module go to step 7
2. On one MPC: Disconnect power supply Connector J1
3. Observe if increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If the increase has stopped, the MPC with intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's
ground has been found  skip step 5 and continue to step 6
5. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1 in order for the MPC to resume normal function and go back to
step 2, choosing the next MPC
6. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1  the MPC will resume normal function.
7. Set the MPC in TEST MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the MPC's normal function.
8. Disconnect connections one at a time (from J2 to J85, - NOT J1), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
9. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
10.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
11.Set the MPC in NORNAL MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O

NOTE: 
If a CCU is disconnected or stopped for more than 20 minutes, establishing of emergency lubrication to the affected cylinder is recommended, by fitting of backup lubrication cables from EICU.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Ch20,2150,Engine Side Speed Set->Suprv. Ch20,2150,Engine Side Speed

alarms.effect: The input value is fixed to last valid input and ESC is not possible.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check ESC speed handle cable to CCU1 (Ch20).\n- If active control station is ESC: Change control station.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Ch20,2156,Engine Side Speed Increas->Suprv. Ch20,2156,Engine Side Speed
alarms.long_description: Channel input is out of range.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or
- Sensor failurer, or missing sensor power supply, or
- MPC input failure, or
- For On/Off type sensors the cause can be a missing or wrong supervision resistor (typically 6.8 kOhm).
alarms.effect: The input value is fixed to last valid input and ESC is not possible.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP Alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Check power supply to the sensor (measure voltage between A (negative) and D (positive)). If voltage is OK (18-32 Vdc): Replace sensor.
- Try to Invalidate the signal on the MPC that has raised the alarm. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

If the problem persists: The MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Ch24,8601,Scavenge Air Pressure->Suprv. Ch24,8601,Scavenge Air Press
