alarms.cause:
- Cable Failure, or
- Sensor error, or
- ME-V timing piston stuck, or
- FIVA valve failure
alarms.effect:
- No exhaust valve timing control.
- Pcomp increases if piston is not moving
- Pmax may increase
- The limiter 'Compression pres.' is activated and it will not be possible to run the engine with
scavenge air pressure above the safe limit for running with ME-V failure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- ME-V piston feedback cabling
- FIVA valve 
- Pcomp and Pmax

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->EngineSide/Remote Control Selection->Inconsistent Control Stat. Request
alarms.long_description: The Control Station Switch Logic has detected inconsistent control signal requests. Cabling seem to be ok but values are inconsistent.
alarms.cause:
The control station switch logic expected a high/low combination of the control station request signals.

One of two events has occurred:
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both low.
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both high.
alarms.effect: The ECS retains its manoeuvre place.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check Ch23 CCU1 (Cable ID = 1118 for Local Control).
- Check Ch23 CCU2 (Cable ID = 1130 for Remote Control).
- Check Pressure Switches to see if sensors are  stuck High or Low. Replace faulty switch or cut out faulty sensor.
- If everything is OK: Replace CCU1 or CCU2.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Generator clutch signals deviate
alarms.long_description: Redundant generator clutch state signals deviate.
alarms.cause: - Cabling failure, or\n- Clutch sensor failure, or\n- MPC input failure
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check cabling, or\n- Check clutch sensor, or\n- If the signal is OK while the alarm is present, the MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Dual tacho signals not valid
alarms.long_description: Speed measured on tacho C/D is not valid.
alarms.cause: - Tacho C/ D encoder failure, or \n- Speed measured by tacho C/D deviates too much from speed measured by tacho A/B.
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check tacho C/D sensors, or\n- Check tacho C/D cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.long_description: The watchdog on the MPC has been disabled.
alarms.cause: Wrong setting of the orange DIP-switch on the MPC.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but with watchdogs disabled the MPC may not respond correctly to software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: Check that MPC DIP-switch is enabled (orange switch must be ON).

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Non standard baud rate
alarms.long_description: Baud rate for service terminal is not 9600 Bd.
alarms.cause: Non-standard Baud rate selected
alarms.effect: No, or unreadable output to service terminal.
alarms.suggested_action: Reset blue DIP, and reboot MPC when appropriate.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: Invalid MPC parameters. The MPC cannot start with incorrect parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm appears when the MPC automatically loads the wrong parameter set after MPC replacement.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the MPC is not correct. The exact effect is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the MPC has just been replaced: Wait for automatic software download to complete.\nCheck MPC power supply and fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: The MPC is running an incorrect application program
alarms.cause: MPC is replaced while both MOP A and MOP B are unavailable.
alarms.effect: The ECS may be seriously affected if MPC is runs incorrect software. The exact behaviour is unknown since it also depends on which MPC is involved.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off MPC immediately. When either MOP A or MOP B is operating again, the MPC can be switched on again. When the automatic preparation of the MPC is finished the MPC will operate correctly again.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: The Parameter flash is corrupt.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If problem persist, the unit may be defect.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description:
At system in operation an ongoing ID-key test is made.
The alarm is set when a read byte in the ID-key is not equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
The alarm is reset as soon a read byte in the ID-key is equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
I. e. a problem also exists with the ID-key when the alarm are not set while it has not been acknowledged.
One byte is tested for each second. If the alarm does not reappear in a test cycle of 256 seconds, the fail on the ID-key is not steady.
alarms.cause: The ID-key is defect, is not plugged correct or is missing.
alarms.effect: No operational effect until the next restart.\nIf the ID-key is plugged correct, the persistent data is lost.
alarms.suggested_action: Ensure the ID-key is plugged correct in the system.\nIf plugged correctly and a system restart fails because of problems with the ID-key, replace the ID-key with a new.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power B failure, connector 1C
alarms.long_description: No power on theMPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal C.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply B for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply B is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply A.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power A failure, connector 1B
alarms.long_description: No power on the MPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal B.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply A for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply A is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply B.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F12 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 12 is blown. Fuse 12 protects the sensor power supply, terminal 'D', of the analogue inputs, channels 20 to 37, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the sensors and signals connected to channels 20 to 37 may give wrong values, and a number of supervision alarms may occur simultaneously.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 20 to 37. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F13 failure
alarms.long_description:
Fuse 13 is blown. Fuse 13 protects the power outlets of:
channels 40 to 47, terminal 'D', 
channels 48 to 53, terminal 'E',
channels 60 and 61, terminal 'H'.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the signals related to channels 40 to 61 may be wrong. Effect on engine behaviour is unknown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for possible failures in the external cabling to channels 40 to 61. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F14 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 14 is blown. Fuse 14 protects the power supply for the analog output, channels 70 and 71, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: Injections will not occur on cylinders controlled by this MPC.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 70 and 71. Replace the fuse. If the fuse blows again: Replaced the MPC.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F9 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 9 is blown. Fuse 9 protects power supply connector 9 of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: Injections will not occur on cylinders controlled by this MPC.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to connector 9. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->System->Battery Level Low
alarms.long_description: MPC battery level low.
alarms.cause: Battery discharged.
alarms.effect: If MPC remains switched on, there is no effect. If the MPC is switched off or power is lost, the MPC will loose its time settings. Time settings will be automatically retrieved at next power on.
alarms.suggested_action:
At next engine stop:
 1) Remove power supply on MPC.
 2) Replace battery.
 3) Reconnect power supply.

alarms.synopsis: EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->EICU Commands->EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.long_description: CCU's receive commands from the EICU at regular intervals. The commands have been missing a number of times.
alarms.cause:
If all CCU's and ETU's report this alarm
- EICU Failure.

If alarm is released randomly from different CCU's and ETU's:
- Network failure.
alarms.effect:
- Engine remains operative. No load reduction required.
- Both ECR and RCS Control stations are no longer available. Only ESC can be used in this situation.
- Speedsetpoint will be 'locked in last' until ESC has been selected.
- Loss of remote control will be displayed on the RCS.
- Set point to and supervision of HPS is lost. The HPS will go to failsafe pressure level (if EIUC power is lost).
- Connection to alarm system is no longer available. Alarms are still displayed on MOP.
- Cylinder lubrication will be set to fail safe amount and lubrication will be speed proportional.
- Several values on the MOP display will be unavailable.
- HPS Slave pump is started (J80 = OFF) regardless of engine load, until the alarm condition is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCU's and ETU's permanently report this alarm: Check EICU:
- Check that the EICU is in normal mode (green LED on MPC)
- Replace EICU with new MPC.

If CCU's and ETU's randomly report this alarm:
- Check network status on MOP maintenance screen.
- Check for ground failure.
- Check all network cabling including terminating resistors.
- Check cable diagram for location of resistors.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Noise Detection Supervision->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the ECS system
alarms.cause:
- One or more ECS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or
- ECS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source

NOTE: 
Unless IRM module is used, the location of a ECS component causing the alarm is NOT limited to the MPC on which the alarm has appeared.
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the ECS system, e.g. 
- Exh. Valve Closed Position Changed
- Exh. Valve closing/opening too fast/slow (4 alarms)
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Total noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, MPCs for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Stop engine or reduce rpm to slow down level
If the MPC is equipped with IRM Module go to step 7
2. On one MPC: Disconnect power supply Connector J1
3. Observe if increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If the increase has stopped, the MPC with intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's
ground has been found  skip step 5 and continue to step 6
5. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1 in order for the MPC to resume normal function and go back to
step 2, choosing the next MPC
6. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1  the MPC will resume normal function.
7. Set the MPC in TEST MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the MPC's normal function.
8. Disconnect connections one at a time (from J2 to J85, - NOT J1), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in total noise pulse counter has stopped
9. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
10.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
11.Set the MPC in NORNAL MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O

NOTE: 
If a CCU is disconnected or stopped for more than 20 minutes, establishing of emergency lubrication to the affected cylinder is recommended, by fitting of backup lubrication cables from EICU.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Tacho->Tacho set A->Tacho set A failure
alarms.long_description: Faulty or missing Tacho signals.
alarms.cause:
- Wiring, sensors or encoders are faulty, or
- Damaged tacho amplifier (loose connections in box, or.
- Loose connections in cable ends, or
- Damaged sensor support console, or
- Damaged teeth on tacho wheel (if fitted) , or
- Power failure (CCU1 powers Tacho Set A and CCU2 powers Tacho Set B).
alarms.effect:
The MPC had to change active set of tacho sensors. 
If both tacho sensor set A and B fail on one CCU:  
- Injection is stopped on one or two cylinders. 
- Cylinder lubrication is stopped on affected cylinders!
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCUs report tacho failure:
- Fault is most likely found in encoder/trigger ring sensors, amplifier or amplifier related cabling.
- If Tacho A reports the problem: Check flywheel sensor.

If only one CCU reports tacho failure:
- Check diode flash pattern (Ch40-Ch47) on MPC and compare to normally working CCU. This will verify CCU and cable connections.

If both Tacho Set A and B reports tacho failure:
- Backup lubrication cables MUST be mounted on affected cylinders.

If all signals on one tacho stay low:
- Check tacho sensor power. 
Hint: All sensor signals toggle between zero and high at least once per revolution.

To troubleshoot the problem: Perform tacho test on MOP:
- Navigate to Maintenance -> Function Test screen.
- Perform Tacho tests and follow instruction.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Suprv. Ch34,2002-B,Shut Down
alarms.long_description: Cable failure.\nNote that the shutdown signal is routed through the ELFI  pilot valve.\nThe signal from the switch connected to the specified channel is out of range. The cabling and the connection to the switch are supervised by an 18 kOhm resistor mounted across the switch in the safety system (Relay in safety system).
alarms.cause: - Failure in the cabling to the switch, or\n- Missing supervision resistor across the switch, or \n- MPC input failure
alarms.effect: - No shutdown. ELFI valve will not respond to shut down from safety system.\n- If the CCU is controlling 2 cylinders the fuel injection on both cylinders will be stopped when required as long as it receives correct redundant shut down signal from safety system.\n- Note: Stop signals can still be used to stop fuel injection.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check cabling and 18 kOhm supervision resistor.\n- Check ELFI pilot valve.\n- Check MPC input.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->IO Terminals->Inconsistent Stop Signals
alarms.long_description: The two redundant Stop signals used by the CCU do not have the same value.
alarms.cause: CCU Hard Wired and CCU from control network have transmitted inconsistent stop signals
alarms.effect:
Engine remains operative. No load reduction required.

Effects:
- Stop signals redundancy is lost.
alarms.suggested_action:
If Engine Running on Fuel:
- All stop sensors must measure a pressure less than 0.5 bar. This can be checked on the MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen Ch36 (Cable ID = 1101-x, where x=CCU Number).

If Engine Stopped (No Fuel):
- All stop sensors must measure a pressure above 4 bar. This can be checked on the MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen Ch36 (Cable ID = 1101-x, where x=CCU Number).

- Cut out faulty sensor.
- Replace faulty sensor  
- If pressure level is low near sensors: Check pipes and fittings for leaks

Notice redundant stop sensor arrangement:
 CCU1, CCU3, CCU5: Redundant STOP from CCU2 Ch36
 CCU2, CCU4, CCU6: Redundant STOP from CCU1 Ch36

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Cylinder Lubrication->Alpha Lubricator A->Failing Lubr. FeedBack (Slowdown)
alarms.long_description: The actuator piston is not moving as expected.
alarms.cause:
- Lubricator pilot valve failure, or
- Activation signal to solinoide missing, or
- Internal lubricator failure, or
- Feedback sensor not working, or
- Hydraulic pressure lost. Valve(s) 560 are closed.
alarms.effect: - Slowdown request is send from ECS.\n- No cylinder lubrication on the affected cylinder.\n- ECS will keep attempting to activate the injector electrically.
alarms.suggested_action:
LED in lubricator solinoide plug flashes:
- Check that valve(s) 560 are open.
- Replace lubricator with a spare.

If the problem persists:
- Check cable between lubricator and MPC.
- If cable path OK: Replace MPC.

LED in lubricator solinoide plug don't flash:
- Check cable path from MPC to solinoide plug.
- If cable path OK: Replace MPC

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Cylinder Lubrication->Alpha Lubricator A->No Cyl. Lube Oil Supply (Slowdown)
alarms.long_description: Cylinder lubrication level switch reports missing cylinder oil.
alarms.cause: - Cylinder lubrication oil supply blocked, or\n- Sensor malfunction, or\n- Electric trace heater off.
alarms.effect: - No cylinder lubrication oil on the affected cylinder.\n- Slowdown request is ordered from ECS.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check that individual shut off valves are not closed.
- Check cylinder lubrication oil tank level.
- Check that heat tracer is on.
- Disassemble pipes and check if cylinder oil still flows.

If the problem persists:
- Replace lubricator level switch.

alarms.synopsis: Cyl. A Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Speed Controller->Cyl. A Running on Backup Telegram
alarms.long_description: The Governor is calculating a Fuel Index based on a backup telegram. This will occur in case of CCU failure.
alarms.cause: The CCU which should send the primary telegram is not on the control network or has stopped running, or \nControl Network problems caused prolonged transfer times.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but Mean Indicated Pressure may drift on affected cylinder.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Measure Mean Indicated Pressure using a PMI system to ensure that the cylinders are balanced. If necessary, adjust mean indicated pressure on MOP.
- Check that all CCUs are running and on the control network. Look for related alarms on MOP.

If the alarm persists during normal running note Engine RPM and direction and contact MAN Diesel when convenient

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Fuel Index Limiters->Torque Limiter->Dynamic Torque Limiter->Dynamic Torque Limiter Time Out
alarms.long_description: Dynamic torque limiter time out
alarms.cause: This alarm indicates that the engine have used the dynamic torque limiter for as long time as allowed
alarms.effect: The torque limiter will decrease to the limiter level allowed for continous operation
alarms.suggested_action: Pressing 'Increase limits' will disregard the time limitations and increase the limiter level to the same level as normally allowed by the dynamic torque limiter. This is not recommend for continuous operation

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->Fuel Index Limiters->Hydraulic Supply Pressure Limiter->Low Hydraulic Pressure
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic supply pressure has dropped. To compensate for insufficient pump flow maximum allowed fuel index is reduced. Fuel index reduction leads to lower hydraulic oil consumption.
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic supply Pump failure, or\n- Hydraulic leakage or failing bypass valves in the hydraulic supply system, or\n- One or more hydraulic supply pumps stopped.
alarms.effect: Engine load might be reduced and engine might run with unstable speed and fuel index. \n\n- If the pressure drops below a predefined level fuel injection is stopped.
alarms.suggested_action:
While locating the failure that causes the pressure drop: Reduce engine load to avoid unstable running. 

- Check for hydraulic pump related alarms. 
- Check for hydraulic leakages, pressure relief valve and failing bypass valves. Typically a failing bypass valve increases significantly in temperature.

Engine Stopped:
- Cut out individual HCU's to determine the location of the  leakage.
- Check the hydraulic pressure decay times on Auxiliaries -> Hydraulic System screen. Compare to reference.

alarms.synopsis: STOP Low While Engine Not Running
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Governor->STOP Low While Engine Not Running
alarms.long_description: Pneumatic STOP signals are off while the engine is stopped. \nSTOP signals are measured by one pressure sensor on each CCU.\nThe pressure sensors are activated by control air supply and connected to CCUs Channel 36.
alarms.cause: - Loss of control air pressure, or\n- Engine stopped unexpectedly.
alarms.effect: If a start attempt is made while this alarm is present air and fuel may be applied simultaneously. This might damage the starting air bursting cap. Avoid Engine start.
alarms.suggested_action:
On the Maintenance -> System View I/O screen: Compare pressure measurements on all CCUs (channel 36). 
STOP is on when pressure is above approximately 2 bar. 

If only one CCU reports this failure:
- Check for pipe leakages near pressure sensor. 
- Check pressure sensor.

If all CCUs reports this failure:
- Check control air supply pressure according to instruction manual. 
- Check double non return valve at engine side. This valve is located in Engine Side Console.
- Check for leakages in the control air system.

If engine stopped unexpectedly: Move handle to stop position to clear the alarm.

alarms.synopsis: Max. Time in Pos. Table Reached
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Fuel Injection->Injection Profile 1->Max. Time in Pos. Table Reached
alarms.long_description: Fuel index ordered has resulted in an ELFI close time that is not supported for the current injection profile.
alarms.cause: - Engine running excessively heavy.\n- Fuel quality is poor\n- Profile shaping causing very long delays.
alarms.effect: Maximum time in position table for current injection profile is used. This means that regardless of how much Fuel index is increased Fuel amount into cylinders does not increase.
alarms.suggested_action:
Contact MAN B&W for the following adjustments:
- Increase maximum time in position table
- Injection Profile is too 'weak'. Make injection profile more aggressive.
- Freeze times are too long resulting in large close times.

alarms.cause:
- Failing ELFI/FIVA Valve
-Failing piston feedback sensor,
- Too high friction in ME-V timing unit (too slow),
- Leakages in timing unit (too fast)
alarms.effect: ECS not able to control exhaust valve timing. Deviation on cylinder compression pressure may be present. Risk of too high compression and maximum pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce Engine load to reduce compression and maximum pressure.

Adjust actual compression and maximum pressure on MOP.

Check:
- ELFI/FIVA alarms
- ME-V Piston feedback sensor
- For leakages at timing unit.

Use HCU Events on MOP to compare ME-V piston feedback signal to other units.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->ELFI Valve A->ELFIA Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: The position feedback on the specific injection controlling valve has shown movements that are not physically realistic.
alarms.cause: Typically loose connection in cabling. Malfunction of internal ELFI-feedback electronics can cause out of range feedback signals.
alarms.effect: When the fault is detected injections are stopped until valve is reactivated via the Engine -> Chief Limiters MOP screen.\n\nThis alarm is a trigger member for the HCU Events screen (Maintaince->TroubleShooting). A log of the incident has been recorded and can be used to further analyse the alarm.
alarms.suggested_action:
Fuel injection is reactivated by toggling invalidation of CCU channel 30 (Maintenance -> System View I/O screen), re-enabling fuel injection on the Engine -> Chief Limiters screen, or CCU power off/on. Before doing any of the above check the following due to danger of Cover Lift:
- Check that Maintenance -> System View I/O -> CCUx-Ch30 -> Electrical Value never is out of range (3.5-20.5 mA)
- Inspect entire cabling from CCU to ELFI Valve.
- If cabling is OK and reactivation does not solve the problem: Replace CCU, 
- If CCU replacement does not solve the problem: Replace ELFI Valve and reactivate as described.

During reactivation: Try to feel the dither on the valve (pressure must be sufficiently high, above approx. 180 bar.

alarms.effect: FIVA Control is stopped and causes fuel injection stop.\n\nThis alarm is a trigger member for the HCU Events screen (Maintaince->TroubleShooting). A log of the incident has been recorded and can be used to further analyse the alarm.
alarms.suggested_action: - Contact B&W. Inform Speed, Active Eng Mode, Approximate Load and manoeuvring condition.\n- If the alarm appears during normal running: Replace the MPC.\n- Fuel-injection is reactivated by MPC power off/on (Reset MPC).

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->Shadow Injection Supervision->ELFIA/B Injections Too Close
alarms.long_description: Internal ECS fault situation. An internal calculation was completed too late.
alarms.cause: Very uncertain. A partly failing network can cause significantly increased CPU load on the MPCs leading to unacceptable delays on some calculations.
alarms.effect: Difficult to predict. Often no effect, in other situations unstable operation of fuel injection and lubrication on some cylinders.
alarms.suggested_action:
Contact MAN B&W. Parameter adjustment may be required.
In the meantime: Monitor exhaust gas temperature:
- If temperature OK: Continue running. 
- If temperature not OK: Shut off that cylinder and continue with reduced load and speed.

alarms.synopsis: ELFIA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->ELFIA Feedback Supervision->ELFIA Fault:Main Spool at Drain Pos
alarms.long_description: ELFI main spool is at Tank position when it should not be.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on ELFI pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck ELFI pilot valve.
- ELFI Main Spool is stuck at tank position.
- ELFI pilot valve receives a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 (ELFIA) or Ch71 (ELFIB) always has an output less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: Injection will not occur as long as this situation is present. However injection will automatically start again when cause of alarm is removed.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 ELFI Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check if the ELFI main spool can be moved hydraulically 
- Dithering on the ELFI Valve when pressure is sufficiently high to move ELFI Main Spool (make sure pressure is above 180 bar).

ELFI Valve Test Procedure: (FUEL INJECTION CAN OCCUR)
- Engine stopped 
- Hydraulic pressure must be sufficiently high to move ELFI Main Spool.
- Go to MOP: Maintenance -> System View I/O screen.
- Set MPC that reports the problem in test mode.
- Set Ch70 to 20 mA.
- ELFI Main Spool must go to Injection side.
- Set Ch70 to 4 mA.
- ELFI Main Spool must go to Tank position.

If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- ELFI Valve on affected Cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Fuel And Exhaust->Supervision->ELFIA Feedback Supervision->ELFIA Integrator Saturation
alarms.long_description: The ELFI controller integrator has compensated more than allowed.
alarms.cause:
Can occur if:
- Loose connection on ELFI pilot valve set point.
- Mechanically stuck ELFI pilot valve.
- ELFI Main Spool is stuck at tank or Injection position.
- ELFI pilot valve recieves a Shut Down but CCU does not.
- CCU Ch70 (ELFIA) or Ch71 (ELFIB) always has an output more than 12 mA or always less  than 12 mA.
alarms.effect: ELFI Controller on CCU can no longer compensate completely for position errors. This will most likely affect mean pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Most likely the Parker Pilot valve is not calibrated precisely to compensate for zero overlap differences.

Check the following:
- Ch 70 Parker pilot Valve cabeling (Cable ID = 4107-A).
- Ch 30 ELFI Spool position is reading out valid mA.
- Check that the parker pilot Valve is not stuck or sticking
- Check if the ELFI main spool can be moved hydraulically.
- Testing the pilot valve and ELFI Valve can be checked using Engine stopped procedure, feeling dithering movement when pressure is above approx. 180 bar.


If nothing is wrong with the cables try to replace:
- Parker pilot Valve.
- CCU reporting the problem.
- ELFI Valve on affected Cylinder.

- Cable Failure, or
- Sensor error, or
- ME-V timing piston stuck, or
- FIVA valve failure

- No exhaust valve timing control.
- Pcomp increases if piston is not moving
- Pmax may increase
- The limiter 'Compression pres.' is activated and it will not be possible to run the engine with
scavenge air pressure above the safe limit for running with ME-V failure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- ME-V piston feedback cabling
- FIVA valve

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->EngineSide/Remote Control Selection->Inconsistent Control Stat. Request
alarms.long_description: The Control Station Switch Logic has detected inconsistent control signal requests. Cabling seem to be ok but values are inconsistent.
alarms.cause:
The control station switch logic expected a high/low combination of the control station request signals.

One of two events has occurred:
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both low.
- Local Control Request and Remote Control Request both high.
alarms.effect: The ECS retains its manoeuvre place.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check Ch23 CCU1 (Cable ID = 1118 for Local Control).
- Check Ch23 CCU2 (Cable ID = 1130 for Remote Control).
- Check Pressure Switches to see if sensors are  stuck High or Low. Replace faulty switch or cut out faulty sensor.
- If everything is OK: Replace CCU1 or CCU2.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Generator clutch signals deviate
alarms.long_description: Redundant generator clutch state signals deviate.
alarms.cause: - Cabling failure, or\n- Clutch sensor failure, or\n- MPC input failure
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check cabling, or\n- Check clutch sensor, or\n- If the signal is OK while the alarm is present, the MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU->Power Take Out->Dual tacho signals not valid
alarms.long_description: Speed measured on tacho C/D is not valid.
alarms.cause: - Tacho C/ D encoder failure, or \n- Speed measured by tacho C/D deviates too much from speed measured by tacho A/B.
alarms.effect: - If generator is disengaged, no immediate effect.\n- If generator is engaged, the governor is forced to 'Low gain mode' which may cause reduced governor performance.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check tacho C/D sensors, or\n- Check tacho C/D cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.long_description: MPC watchdog disabled
alarms.cause: Green DIP-switch is set to 'Off'
alarms.effect: No effect on engine performance.\nThe MPC may respond incorrectly to any software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: Set green DIP-switch to 'On'

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->System->Non standard baud rate
alarms.long_description: Service terminal baud rate is not 9600 Bd
alarms.cause: Non-standard Baud rate selected
alarms.effect: No, or unreadable output to service terminal.
alarms.suggested_action: When convenient: Reset Blue DIP switch and reboot MPC

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: The MPC holds invalid parameters. The MPC cannot start its application without the correct parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm is caused from the MPC automatically loads the wrong parameter set after a replacement of the MPC.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the MPC is not correct. The exact effect is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the involved MPC just have been replaced, wait for the automatic preparation to complete. If this\ntakes more than 10 minutes, the LED colour signalling for fault indication should be inspected. If this\nproves unhelpful, reset the MPC unit. If it still does not help, contact MAN B&W Diesel.

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: MPC is running an incorrect application
alarms.cause: MOP A and B not available during MPC power up
alarms.effect: Reduced system performance\nNOTE\nNever ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise!
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off MPC immediately.\nWhen MOP A or MOP B are available: Restart MPC

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: Parameter flash failure
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If problem persist, the unit may be defect.

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description: The MPC cannot read ID-key data
alarms.cause:
- ID-key is not plugged in, or
- ID-key data is corrupted, or
- ID-key hardware failure, or
- MPC failure
alarms.effect: No immediate effect on engine performance.\nThe MPC may not function correctly after a restart.
alarms.suggested_action:
If this alarm is active for more than 5 minutes, check that the ID-key is plugged in correctly.
If the problem persists replace, one at a time:
- ID-key (see instruction manual for configuration instructions)
- MPC

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: LDCL->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level

alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description:
At system in operation an ongoing ID-key test is made.
The alarm is set when a read byte in the ID-key is not equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
The alarm is reset as soon a read byte in the ID-key is equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
I. e. a problem also exists with the ID-key when the alarm are not set while it has not been acknowledged.
One byte is tested for each second. If the alarm does not reappear in a test cycle of 256 seconds, the fail on the ID-key is not steady.
alarms.cause: The ID-key is defect, is not plugged correct or is missing.
alarms.effect: No operational effect until the next restart.\nIf the ID-key is plugged correct, the persistent data is lost.
alarms.suggested_action: Ensure the ID-key is plugged correct in the system.\nIf plugged correctly and a system restart fails because of problems with the ID-key, replace the ID-key with a new.

alarms.synopsis: Net A not connected to EICU
alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->System Status->Net A not connected to EICU
alarms.long_description: Controlling unit not connected to network segment A.
alarms.cause: Network cabling problems.
alarms.effect: If only one network segment alarm is raised: No change in engine behaviour.\nIf both network segment A and B are affected: No or faulty MPC operation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If alarm(s) indicates missing connection to one network segment on one MPC: 
1) Check that network connector is mounted on the unit. 
2) Replace the network connector. 
3) If no problems found in the network connection: Replace the unit.

If alarms indicate missing connection on both network segments on the same MPC: 
1) Check if the unit is turned on: 
1.A) MPC: Indicator LED lamp is illuminated. 
1.B) MOP: Graphic application pictures on the screen. 

If the unit is turned off: Check for power failure. Otherwise: 
MPC related:
1) If the indicator LED lamp of the MPC is green: Check the network connections and connectors of the unit for cabling failures. 
2) Restart the controller, e.g. by turn off - turn on power. 
3) If the controller does not start up, indicated by the LED changing from red to yellow and to green, and the network alarms does not disappear: Replace MPC. 

MOP Related:
1) If the display of the MOP is active with normal application pictures, but process values are missing: Check the network connections and connectors of the unit for cabling failures.
2) Restart the MOP (Ctrl Esc, then press Stop MOP and Quit. Wait a bit and press Ctrl Ecs, then Start MOP). If the MOP does not show application pictures, and the network alarm persists: Repair MOP.

If alarms indicate that several units are not connected on one network segment: Inspect the cabling and all connectors of the specified network segment.The fault is likely related to:
1) A loose wire in a connector
2) A short circuit between the 2 wires, or between a wire and the cable screen.
3) In each end of the network line a resistor shall be mounted in the network connector. One of them may be loose or missing.
4) Short circuit between a network wire and ship ground - any metal parts.
5) Network cable damaged.

alarms.synopsis: Net A not connected to ETU2
alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->System Status->Net A not connected to ETU2
alarms.long_description: Controlling unit not connected to network segment A.
alarms.cause: Network cabling problems.
alarms.effect: If only one network segment alarm is raised: No change in engine behaviour.\nIf both network segment A and B are affected: No or faulty MPC operation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If alarm(s) indicates missing connection to one network segment on one MPC: 
1) Check that network connector is mounted on the unit. 
2) Replace the network connector. 
3) If no problems found in the network connection: Replace the unit.

If alarms indicate missing connection on both network segments on the same MPC: 
1) Check if the unit is turned on: 
1.A) MPC: Indicator LED lamp is illuminated. 
1.B) MOP: Graphic application pictures on the screen. 

If the unit is turned off: Check for power failure. Otherwise: 
MPC related:
1) If the indicator LED lamp of the MPC is green: Check the network connections and connectors of the unit for cabling failures. 
2) Restart the controller, e.g. by turn off - turn on power. 
3) If the controller does not start up, indicated by the LED changing from red to yellow and to green, and the network alarms does not disappear: Replace MPC. 

MOP Related:
1) If the display of the MOP is active with normal application pictures, but process values are missing: Check the network connections and connectors of the unit for cabling failures.
2) Restart the MOP (Ctrl Esc, then press Stop MOP and Quit. Wait a bit and press Ctrl Ecs, then Start MOP). If the MOP does not show application pictures, and the network alarm persists: Repair MOP.

If alarms indicate that several units are not connected on one network segment: Inspect the cabling and all connectors of the specified network segment.The fault is likely related to:
1) A loose wire in a connector
2) A short circuit between the 2 wires, or between a wire and the cable screen.
3) In each end of the network line a resistor shall be mounted in the network connector. One of them may be loose or missing.
4) Short circuit between a network wire and ship ground - any metal parts.
5) Network cable damaged.

alarms.long_description: The controlling unit is not connected to network segment B.
alarms.cause: Network cabling problems.
alarms.effect: If only one network segment alarm is raised: No change in engine behaviour.\nIf both network segment A and B are affected: No or faulty MPC operation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If alarm(s) indicates missing connection to one network segment on one MPC: 
1) Check that network connector is mounted on the unit. 
2) Replace the network connector. 
3) If no problems found in the network connection: Replace the unit.

If alarms indicate missing connection on both network segments on the same MPC: 
1) Check if the unit is turned on: 
1.A) MPC: Indicator LED lamp is illuminated. 
1.B) MOP: Graphic application pictures on the screen. 

If the unit is turned off: Check for power failure. Otherwise: 
MPC related:
1) If the indicator LED lamp of the MPC is green: Check the network connections and connectors of the unit for cabling failures. 
2) Restart the controller, e.g. by turn off - turn on power. 
3) If the controller does not start up, indicated by the LED changing from red to yellow and to green, and the network alarms does not disappear: Replace MPC. 

MOP Related:
1) If the display of the MOP is active with normal application pictures, but process values are missing: Check the network connections and connectors of the unit for cabling failures.
2) Restart the MOP (Ctrl Esc, then press Stop MOP and Quit. Wait a bit and press Ctrl Ecs, then Start MOP). If the MOP does not show application pictures, and the network alarm persists: Repair MOP.

If alarms indicate that several units are not connected on one network segment: Inspect the cabling and all connectors of the specified network segment.The fault is likely related to:
1) A loose wire in a connector
2) A short circuit between the 2 wires, or between a wire and the cable screen.
3) In each end of the network line a resistor shall be mounted in the network connector. One of them may be loose or missing.
4) Short circuit between a network wire and ship ground - any metal parts.
5) Network cable damaged.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->System Status->HSU3 unavailable
alarms.long_description: EICU cannot detect unit on either of the networks (segment A and B).
alarms.cause:
- No power to the unit, or
- Network cables are disconnected from the unit, or
- Network cables to the unit are damaged, or 
- Terminating resistor missing.
alarms.effect: No effect.
alarms.suggested_action:
MOPA and/or MOPB:
- Check that the unit(s) are turned on and that the control network is properly connected.

MPC (EICU, SCU or CCU's):
- Check that the LED indication on MPC is on and NOT Red. If LED is Red: Reset MPC. 
- Check that the control network is properly connected and cables not damaged.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->System Status->App. not running on HSU4
alarms.long_description: The MPC is not in normal running mode. The EICU monitors all MPCs.
alarms.cause: Power loss or MPC reboot. \nThe alarm appears shortly after MPC power up. It disappears automatically when MPC is in normal mode.
alarms.effect: - Unable to simulate feedback for ELFIA and ELFIB\n- Unable to simulate feedbacksignals for Lubricator A and B
alarms.suggested_action: If the MPC has just been replaced: Wait for automatic software download to complete.\nCheck MPC power supply and fuse.

 1) Remove power supply on MPC.

alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:

- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or

- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced

NOTE:

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->IO Terminals->EEXI Load Limiter Interface->EEXI Load Limit Cancelled
alarms.long_description: EEXI Load Limitation is cancelled and is therefore not in effect.
alarms.cause: The cancel command is activated on the bridge or the cancel command signal is failing.
alarms.effect: EEXI Load Limitation is not in effect.\nIn case of signal failure, the limitation is automatically cancelled as a fail safe mode.
alarms.suggested_action:
In case the limitation is manually cancelled:
- The EEXI Load Limitation should only be cancelled for the purpose of securing the safety of the ship or saving life at sea, consistent with regulation 3.1 of MARPOL Annex VI (e.g. operating in adverse weather and ice-infested waters, participation in search and rescue operations, avoidance of pirates and engine maintenance). Deactivate the cancel command as soon as the imminent situation is over.
- It must be logged in the Onboard Management Manual for the EEXI Engine Load Limitation whenever the limitation is cancelled.

In case of signal failure:
- Check the alarm info for the failing signal, or
- EICU controller is not in normal mode.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->IO Terminals->EEXI Load Limiter Interface->EEXI Lim Exceeded - Not Cancelled
alarms.long_description: The engine load is above the EEXI Load Limit without manual cancellation of the EEXI Load Limitation.
alarms.cause: This situation arises because the propulsion control system orders too high propeller pitch or engine speed.
alarms.effect: EEXI Load Limitation is exceeded.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Manually reduce the propeller pitch set point or the engine speed set point.
- Check the Near Limit or the Index Margin cable and connectors (from EICU controller) to the propulsion control system.
- Check the propulsion control system reacts on the Near Limit or Index Margin signal sent from the engine control system.
- It must be logged in the Onboard Management Manual for the EEXI Engine Load Limitation whenever the limitation is cancelled.

alarms.cause: - MPC failure (ETU, Exhaust valve timing unit), or\n- ETU power failure, or\n- ETU network failure
alarms.effect:
Normal operation of the engine not affected in Ahead direction.

For Astern operation:
- Increaed Pcomp on all cylinders
- Increased torsional vibrations
alarms.suggested_action:

Check:
- ETU
- ETU Power and network cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->IO Terminals->Ch20,2140,ECR Speed Set Point->Suprv. Ch20,2140,ECR Speed Set Poin
alarms.long_description: Channel input is out of range.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or
- Sensor failurer, or missing sensor power supply, or
- MPC input failure, or
- For On/Off type sensors the cause can be a missing or wrong supervision resistor (typically 6.8 kOhm).
alarms.effect: The Engine Control System uses the latest valid value.\nAny changes of the input will have no effect while this alarm is active.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP Alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Check power supply to the sensor (measure voltage between A (negative) and D (positive)). If voltage is OK (18-32 Vdc): Replace sensor.
- Try to Invalidate the signal on the MPC that has raised the alarm. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

If the problem persists: The MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Hydraulic Power Supply->HPS Setpoint Error Supervision->Hyd. Pressure Set Point deviation
alarms.long_description: The automatic pressure control could not achieve correct pressure
alarms.cause: HPS pumps do not deliver the pressure as expected or leakage has increased or electrical connection to HPS is failing
alarms.effect: - Too low pressure may reduce injections and slow down the engine - in extreme cases stop the engine\n- Too high pressure can result in excessive electrical power consumption
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to HPS (e.g. using manual control). 
Check pressure sensor. 
Check for hydraulic leakages.
Check Swash Plate Indicators.
Check that there are no other alarms for Pumps missing.
Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position.
Check EICU J80 relay:
    a) Off then 'Slave' pump should be running.
    b) ON then 'Slave' pump should be stopped.

If all checks above are ok, the HPS proportional valve may need to be recalibrated.

NOTE: 
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to 'Pump 1 Master' or 'Pump 2 Master'. If the switch is in 'Pump 1 & 2' then both HPS pumps should run.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Hydraulic Power Supply->Slave Pump Run/Stop->Master/Slave Pump Not Running
alarms.long_description: The Engine Control System (ECS) expects more pumps to run but only zero or one 'Running' signal is currently present.
alarms.cause: - Could be caused by wrong running signal or failed pump(s).\n- Could be wrong switch settings on the HPS starter cabinet.
alarms.effect: - No effect if both HPS pumps are running.\n- If only one pump is running the maximum obtainable load will be limited depending on engine configuration. Normally minimum 55% engine load should be possible.\n- If no pumps are running the engine will stop.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Move the HPS Slave pump control switch to 'Pump 1 & 2' on the HPS starter cabinet, while troubleshooting. This will prevent the ECS from starting/stopping the slave pump untill the error has been identified and corrected. In case this is not desirable repeated start/stop of the slave pump can be expected.

- Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position. Position are either 
1) Pump 1 Master (Pump 2 controlled by EICU J80 On = STOP)
2) Pump 1 & 2 (Both Pumps running)
3) Pump 2 Master (Pump 1 controlled by EICU J80 On = STOP)

- Check the HPS pumps and verify that both pumps are not running. If they are both running a failure in one of the running signal is present. Check cabling to Pump 1 and Pump 2 running signals.
(EICU J31 Pump 1 Running signal)
(EICU J34 Pump 2 Running signal).

- Check cabling for EICU J80 relay:
    a) Off then 'Slave' pump should be running.
    b) ON then 'Slave' pump should be stopped.

NOTE: 
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to Pump 1 Master or Pump 2 Master. If the switch is in 'Pump 1 & 2' position then both HPS pumps should always run.

alarms.synopsis: Slave Pump Started Due to Error(s)
alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Hydraulic Power Supply->Slave Pump Run/Stop->Slave Pump Started Due to Error(s)
alarms.long_description: Normally the ECS only starts the Slave pump when the engine load is above a certain limit. In case of certain errors the Slave pump is ordered started (EICU J80 Off)
alarms.cause:
- Hydraulic Pressure is not valid
- Internal load calculation is not valid (CCU1 failure?).
- Setpoint too high compared to actual pressure (Alarm for 'Hydr. Press. Regulator High Fail' could also be present!)
- Missing Pump (Master/Slave pump switched off or missing valid running signals.)
alarms.effect: - No effect if both HPS pumps are running.\n- If only one pump is running the maximum obtainable load will be limited depending on engine configuration. Normally minimum 55% engine load should be possible.\n- If no pumps are running the engine will stop.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Move the HPS Slave pump control switch to 'Pump 1 & 2' on the HPS starter cabinet, while troubleshooting. This will prevent the ECS from starting/stopping the slave pump untill the error has been identified and corrected. In case this is not desirable repeated start/stop of the slave pump can be expected.

- Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position. Position are either 
1) Pump 1 Master (Pump 2 controlled by EICU J80 On = STOP)
2) Pump 1 & 2 (Both Pumps running)
3) Pump 2 Master (Pump 1 controlled by EICU J80 On = STOP)

- Depending on the type of error that caused this alarm to be raised check the following:
a) Cabling to Hydraulic pressure sensor EICU J30.
b) Network or tacho alarms on MOP from CCU1.
c) Hydraulic Pressure Setpoint deviation too large compared to measured pressure.
D) Missing pump running signals.

- Check the HPS pumps and verify that both pumps are not running. If they are both running a failure in one or both running signals ares present. Check cabeling to Pump 1 and Pump 2 running signals.
(EICU J31 Pump 1 Running signal)
(EICU J34 Pump 2 Running signal).

- Check cabling for EICU J80 relay:
    a) Off then 'Slave' pump should be running.
    B) ON then 'Slave' pump should be stopped.

NOTE: 
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to Pump 1 as slave or Pump 2 as slave. If the switch is in No Slave position then both HPS pumps should always run.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Hydraulic Power Supply->Hydraulic Pressure fell too quickly
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic pressure fell too quickly after all pumps were stopped.
alarms.cause: Hydraulic leakage or failing accumulator(s).
alarms.effect: Hydraulic leakage or failing accumulators may cause problems when the engine is started again. Correct these failures before attempting normal running.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for Hydraulic leakage and check accumulator pressure.\n- Investigate all HCU's by cutting off relevant valves. Do this one HCU at a time and evaluate leakage result.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Hydraulic Power Supply->Manual Hydr. Press Control
alarms.long_description: HPS pressure control is manual
alarms.cause: Manual Activated
alarms.effect:
The HPS will 'bumpless' change to Manual operation. The pressure setpoint can be overruled by the operator by manually altering the pressure setpoint. The new pressure setpoint will be used until the operator either selects a new setpoint, or returns to Automatic mode.

NOTE: 
A large increase in setpoint could trigger the HPS slave pump to start. Therefore it is recommended to limit the steps to about 20 bar.
alarms.suggested_action:
Switch to Automatic operation when manual operation is ended.

NOTE:
In case the ECS setpoint in automatic operation is more than 20 bar above the manual setpoint, increase the manual pressure setpoint, before switching out of manual operation.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Hydraulic Power Supply->Pump 1 not Running
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic pump should run because the engine is running.
alarms.cause: The pump does not give a 'Running' signal.
alarms.effect: - Maximum engine load is limited if pump is not running.\n- The Engine Control System (ECS) have ordered the HPS slave pump to start (J80 = OFF). The slave pump will be running until both Pump running signals have been detected On.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check if the pump is running.\n- if it is running check the cable giving a 'Running' signal to ECS.\n- In case the Pump running signal turns On/Off and triggers the slave pump to start/stop go to the HPS starter cabinets and move switch to 'Pump 1 & 2'. alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->ECR/RCS Control Selection->Inconsistent Control Stat. Request
alarms.long_description: The Control Station Switch Logic has detected inconsistent control signal requests. Cabling seem to be ok but values are inconsistent.
alarms.cause:
The control station switch logic expected a high/low combination of the control station request signals.

One of two events has occurred:
- ECR Request and RCS Request both low.
- ECR Request and RCS Request both high.
alarms.effect: The ECS retains its manoeuvre place.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling between EICU and manoeuvre places. 
-  Ch22 on EICU is ECR Control (Cable ID = 2121)
-  Ch25 on EICU is RCS Control (Cable ID = 2122)
- Replace faulty switch or cut out faulty sensor.
If the problem persists:  Replace EICU.

alarms.synopsis: No Cyl. Lube Oil due to CCU Failure
alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->ECS Slow Down Request->No Cyl. Lube Oil due to CCU Failure
alarms.long_description: No cylinder lubrication for the affected cylinder(s).
alarms.cause: - The Cylinder Control Unit is not in normal running mode.\n- The ECS control networks are not connected properly or not working.
alarms.effect: - Probably no cylinder lubrication oil is injected to the cylinder(s).\n- Slow Down request is send from ECS to the slow down system.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check that the LED is green on affected CCU.
- If the LED is NOT green: Rreboot the CCU. 
If the problem persists: Replace  the MPC.

- If the LED IS green: Use MOP Network status screen to check for network status. Often the only way to find and correct network problems is to inspect entire network cabling and check for ground failure on ECS power supply.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->ECS Slow Down Request->Slow Down Request
alarms.long_description: Slow Down Request
alarms.cause: ECS requested Slow Down due to failing cylinder oil lubrication or VT/Bypass problems.
alarms.effect: - No cylinder lubricator oil injected. This will lead to excessive liner wear.\n- Too High Pscav can damage Engine or Turbocharger.
alarms.suggested_action: Check alarm list and follow suggested action.

alarms.synopsis: No Exh. timing due to CCU Failure

alarms.effect:
- No exhaust valve timing control. 
- Pcomp may increase
- Pmax may increase 
- The limiter 'Compression pres.' may be activated and it will not be possible to run the engine with scavenge air pressure above the safe limit for running with ME-V failure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check that the LED is green on affected CCU.
- If the LED is NOT green: Rreboot the CCU. 
If the problem persists: Replace  the MPC.

- If the LED IS green: Use MOP Network status screen to check for network status. Often the only way to find and correct network problems is to inspect entire network cabling and check for ground failure on ECS power supply.

alarms.long_description: CCU not in Normal mode or not on the network

alarms.effect: - The limiter 'Compression pres.' may be activated and it will not be possible to run the engine with scavenge air pressure above the safe limit for running with ME-V failure.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check MPC is in Normal mode\n- Check cabling, fuses and power\n- If the problem persists: Replace CCU

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Load Reduction Supervision->Pmax Supervision->Average Pmax above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Average Pmax has exceeded Pmax alarm limit.
alarms.cause: Too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect:
- Activation of Compression pressure limiter (if Pscav above safety limit)
- Increased wear of cylinder liners
- Risk of breakage of piston rings
- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce 'Pmax Offset All' to lower average Pmax below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that 'Estimated Engine Load' (as shown on MOP) is correct by comparing with PMI equipment and/or torquemeter. 
If incorrect then utilize Fuel Quality feature for adjusting estimated engine load.
2.Check that average 'Current Pcomp' and 'Ordered Pcomp' are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing 'Pcomp/Pscav Offset All' manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp mean value).
3.Check that average 'Current Pmax' and 'Ordered Pmax' are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing 'Pmax Offset All' manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax mean value).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then Pscav might be too high. This could be due to severe ambient conditions or malfunctioning of exhaust gas bypass etc. Please do not use Auto Tuning functionality and keep 'Pmax Offset All' reduced manually below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Load Reduction Supervision->Pmax Supervision->Cyl 1. Pmax above allowed value

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Engine Running Mode->ME-V Commissioning Mode Active
alarms.long_description: ME-V Commissioning Mode is active.
alarms.cause: The ME-V Commissioning Mode has been activated.
alarms.effect: The desired ME-V effect is determined by the ME-V Commissioning Mode parameter and thus, not the ME-V Effect table.\n\nFurthermore the Pcomp/Pscav Ratio Adjustment is disabled.
alarms.suggested_action: This alarm is allowed to be active during commissioning of ME-V.\n\nAfter finishing the commissioning of ME-V, deactivate the ME-V Commissioning Mode.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->Engine Running Mode->Active EngRunMode Not Calibrated
alarms.long_description: Active Engine Running Mode is currently not calibrated.
alarms.cause:
The calibration engine Load for Active Engine Running Mode has not been completed.
While the engine is on the test bed and the calibration of the Engine Running Mode is not
completed this Alarm will occur. Calibration of engine running mode must be completed,
and alarm must be cleared, before delivery test.
alarms.effect: Engine Load calculation has reduced accuracy in this mode, which may result in engine overload or\ninsufficient power delivery.
alarms.suggested_action: This Alarm will go away upon completion calibration of all load point in Active Engine Running Mode.\nThis alarm should only occur while the engine is on test bed and during commission.\nIf this alarm occurs while the engine is in service contact the engine builder.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->ContinuousTuning PI (online FQA)->Online FQA exceeds limits
alarms.long_description: The difference between ordered Govenor Index and estimated Index (from PMI system) has exceeded the allowed limit.
alarms.cause: Fuel quality has changed since last manual adjustment of Fuel Quality. \n- If WIF(Water In Fuel) is applied to engine the Water content may have changed.
alarms.effect: The Engine load estimation is not fully correct anymore - this may give problems with fuel limiters.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Manual adjustment of Fuel Quality is correct (MOP->Engine->Process Adjustment->Fuel Quality Adjustment)
- PI values on PMI system. 

If problem is not solved by this:
- Note down difference in Engine load for later trouble-shooting (PMI system and ME-ECS (MOP->Engine->Process values->Running Mode)).  
- Adjust 'applied fuel quality offset' manually (hand tuning) until online correction is in range 
 - OR
- Disable Online correction on MOP (MOP->Engine->Process Adjustment->Fuel Quality Adjustment)

alarms.effect: - Fuel Index is not automatically corrected\n- Offline correction value is used\n- Engine operation is not optimal in this condition
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to Automatic Mode as soon as manual operation is completed

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Sensor Supervision->Sensor Values from PMI not Valid
alarms.long_description: Sensor values received from PMI Auto-tuning are not valid.
alarms.cause:
Could be caused by:
- PMI Pressure Sensor error
- PMI Auto-tuning Program is not running
- MOPB is not running
- The program for transferring values from the PMI Auto-tuning program to MOPB has stopped running
- PMI Auto-tuning PC has lost network connection to MOPB
alarms.effect: Auto Tuning is no longer available. Continuous Auto Tuning has been disabled.\nECS alarms for too high Pmax, too high Prise and alarm for Cylinder pressure deviation are no longer available.\nEngine balancing and load distribution might be effected.
alarms.suggested_action:

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Sensor Supervision->Cylinder pressure deviation
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure measurement deviates more from average value than alarm limit.
alarms.cause:
Could be caused by malfunctioning of:
- PMI Pressure Sensor
- Fuel valves
- Exhaust valve
- Suction valve
- Exhaust valve actuator
- FIVA valve
- Fuel booster
- HCU Accumulators
alarms.effect: Auto Tuning is no longer available. Continuous Auto Tuning has been disabled.\nECS alarms for too high Pmax, too high Prise and alarm for Cylinder pressure deviation are no longer available.\nEngine balancing and load distribution might be effected.
alarms.suggested_action: Carry out troubleshooting on above mentioned equipment.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Prise Supervision->Average Prise above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Average Prise has exceeded Pmax-Pcomp alarm limit.
alarms.cause: Too low Compression Pressure or too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce 'Pmax Offset All' to lower average Prise below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that 'Estimated Engine Load' (as shown on MOP) is correct by comparing with PMI equipment and/or torquemeter. 
If incorrect then utilize Fuel Quality feature for adjusting estimated engine load.
2.Check that average 'Current Pcomp' and 'Ordered Pcomp' are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing 'Pcomp/Pscav Offset All' manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp mean value).
3.Check that average 'Current Pmax' and 'Ordered Pmax' are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing Pmax Offset All manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax mean value).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then Pscav might be too low. This could be due to severe ambient conditions or malfunctioning of exhaust gas bypass etc. Please do not use Auto Tuning functionality and keep 'Pmax Offset All' reduced manually below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Prise Supervision->Cyl 1. Prise above allowed value

alarms.suggested_action:
