alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Pmax Supervision->Cyl 12. Pmax above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Pmax has exceeded alarm limit.
alarms.cause: Too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce 'Pmax Offset' on actual cylinder unit to lower Pmax below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that current Pcomp 'Deviation' for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances.
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing 'Pcomp/Pscav Offset' on the actual cylinder unit manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp Deviation ->Pcomp).
2.Check that current Pmax 'Deviation' for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances.
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing 'Pmax Offset' for the actual cylinder unit manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax Deviation ->Pmax).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then please do not use Auto Tuning functionality and keep 'Pmax Offset' reduced manually on actual cylinder unit below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.long_description: The watchdog on the MPC has been disabled.
alarms.cause: Wrong setting of the orange DIP-switch on the MPC.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, but with watchdogs disabled the MPC may not respond correctly to software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: Check that MPC DIP-switch is enabled (orange switch must be ON).

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->Non standard baud rate
alarms.long_description: Baud rate for service terminal is not 9600 Bd.
alarms.cause: Non-standard Baud rate selected
alarms.effect: No, or unreadable output to service terminal.
alarms.suggested_action: Reset blue DIP, and reboot MPC when appropriate.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: Invalid MPC parameters. The MPC cannot start with incorrect parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm appears when the MPC automatically loads the wrong parameter set after MPC replacement.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the MPC is not correct. The exact effect is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the MPC has just been replaced: Wait for automatic software download to complete.\nCheck MPC power supply and fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: The MPC is running an incorrect application program
alarms.cause: MPC is replaced while both MOP A and MOP B are unavailable.
alarms.effect: The ECS may be seriously affected if MPC is runs incorrect software. The exact behaviour is unknown since it also depends on which MPC is involved.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off MPC immediately. When either MOP A or MOP B is operating again, the MPC can be switched on again. When the automatic preparation of the MPC is finished the MPC will operate correctly again.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: The Parameter flash is corrupt.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If problem persist, the unit may be defect.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description:
At system in operation an ongoing ID-key test is made.
The alarm is set when a read byte in the ID-key is not equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
The alarm is reset as soon a read byte in the ID-key is equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
I. e. a problem also exists with the ID-key when the alarm are not set while it has not been acknowledged.
One byte is tested for each second. If the alarm does not reappear in a test cycle of 256 seconds, the fail on the ID-key is not steady.
alarms.cause: The ID-key is defect, is not plugged correct or is missing.
alarms.effect: No operational effect until the next restart.\nIf the ID-key is plugged correct, the persistent data is lost.
alarms.suggested_action: Ensure the ID-key is plugged correct in the system.\nIf plugged correctly and a system restart fails because of problems with the ID-key, replace the ID-key with a new.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->24V power supervision->24V power B failure, connector 1C
alarms.long_description: No power on theMPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal C.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply B for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply B is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply A.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->24V power supervision->24V power A failure, connector 1B
alarms.long_description: No power on the MPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal B.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply A for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply A is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply B.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F12 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 12 is blown. Fuse 12 protects the sensor power supply, terminal 'D', of the analogue inputs, channels 20 to 37, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the sensors and signals connected to channels 20 to 37 may give wrong values, and a number of supervision alarms may occur simultaneously.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 20 to 37. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F13 failure
alarms.long_description:
Fuse 13 is blown. Fuse 13 protects the power outlets of:
channels 40 to 47, terminal 'D', 
channels 48 to 53, terminal 'E',
channels 60 and 61, terminal 'H'.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the signals related to channels 40 to 61 may be wrong. Effect on engine behaviour is unknown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for possible failures in the external cabling to channels 40 to 61. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F14 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 14 is blown. Fuse 14 protects the power supply for the analog output, channels 70 and 71, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: - Electrical overload, or\n- Short circuit
alarms.effect: Signals received on channel J70 and J71 may be faulty.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 70 and 71. Replace the fuse. If the fuse blows again: Replaced the MPC.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F9 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 9 is blown. Fuse 9 protects power supply connector 9 of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: Signals received on channel J9 may be faulty.\nMultiple supervision alarms are raised as a consequence of this condition.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to connector 9. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->System->Battery Level Low
alarms.long_description: MPC battery level low.
alarms.cause: Battery discharged.
alarms.effect: If MPC remains switched on, there is no effect. If the MPC is switched off or power is lost, the MPC will loose its time settings. Time settings will be automatically retrieved at next power on.
alarms.suggested_action:
At next engine stop:
 1) Remove power supply on MPC.
 2) Replace battery.
 3) Reconnect power supply.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->IO Configuration->Ch35,3035,ECS Insulation (kOhm)->Suprv. Ch35,3035,ECS Insulation (kO
alarms.long_description: Sensor signal is out of range
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or
- Sensor failurer, or missing sensor power supply, or
- MPC input failure, or
- For On/Off type sensors the cause can be a missing or wrong supervision resistor (typically 6.8 kOhm).
alarms.effect: Supervision failure for the insulation detection unit will stop all insulation detection.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.synopsis: EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->IO Configuration->EICU Commands->EICU Failed or No Telegram Received
alarms.long_description: ETU receive commands from the EICU at regular intervals. The commands have been missing a number of times.
alarms.cause:
If all CCU's and ETU's report this alarm
- EICU Failure.

If alarm is released randomly from different CCU's and ETU's:
- Network failure.
alarms.effect: - Engine remains operative.\n- Compression pressure may increase too much if engine load increases.\n- Exhaust valve timing will be locked in last.
alarms.suggested_action:
If all CCU's and ETU's permanently report this alarm: Check EICU:
- Check that the EICU is in normal mode (green LED on MPC)
- Replace EICU with new MPC.

If CCU's and ETU's randomly report this alarm:
- Check network status on MOP maintenance screen.
- Check for ground failure.
- Check all network cabling including terminating resistors.
- Check cable diagram for location of resistors.

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: ETU->Cylinder Control Pressure->Cyl 1: CPC Valve Not Open (AH)
alarms.long_description: CPC Valve not open on affected unit.
alarms.cause: - CPC Valve failure, or\n- CPC Valve feedback failure, or\n- MPC or Cable failure
alarms.effect: - Too slow closing of exhaust valve\n- Pcomp and Pmax decreased on affected unit. \n- Misfiring due to low Pcomp may occur.
alarms.suggested_action:
Verify/adjust Pcomp on affected unit. 
In case of misfire then cut out fuel on affected unit.

Check:
- CPC Valve
- CPC Valve Feedback
- MPC and Cabling

alarms.suggested_action:

- CPC Valve feedback

alarms.effect: No, or unreadable output to service terminal.
alarms.suggested_action: Reset blue DIP, and reboot MPC when appropriate.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: Invalid MPC parameters. The MPC cannot start with incorrect parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm appears when the MPC automatically loads the wrong parameter set after MPC replacement.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the MPC is not correct. The exact effect is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the MPC has just been replaced: Wait for automatic software download to complete.\nCheck MPC power supply and fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: The MPC is running an incorrect application program
alarms.cause: MPC is replaced while both MOP A and MOP B are unavailable.
alarms.effect: The ECS may be seriously affected if MPC is runs incorrect software. The exact behaviour is unknown since it also depends on which MPC is involved.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off MPC immediately. When either MOP A or MOP B is operating again, the MPC can be switched on again. When the automatic preparation of the MPC is finished the MPC will operate correctly again.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: The Parameter flash is corrupt.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If problem persist, the unit may be defect.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description:
At system in operation an ongoing ID-key test is made.
The alarm is set when a read byte in the ID-key is not equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
The alarm is reset as soon a read byte in the ID-key is equal to the corresponding value saved in the CPU-RAM.
I. e. a problem also exists with the ID-key when the alarm are not set while it has not been acknowledged.
One byte is tested for each second. If the alarm does not reappear in a test cycle of 256 seconds, the fail on the ID-key is not steady.
alarms.cause: The ID-key is defect, is not plugged correct or is missing.
alarms.effect: No operational effect until the next restart.\nIf the ID-key is plugged correct, the persistent data is lost.
alarms.suggested_action: Ensure the ID-key is plugged correct in the system.\nIf plugged correctly and a system restart fails because of problems with the ID-key, replace the ID-key with a new.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power B failure, connector 1C
alarms.long_description: No power on theMPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal C.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply B for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply B is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply A.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->24V power supervision->24V power A failure, connector 1B
alarms.long_description: No power on the MPC power inlet, connector J1, terminal B.
alarms.cause: - The breaker of power supply A for the specified MPC is turned off. \n- 24V power supply A is turned off. \n- Power cabling is faulty.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect, as the MPC is supplied by power supply B.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for the causes.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F12 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 12 is blown. Fuse 12 protects the sensor power supply, terminal 'D', of the analogue inputs, channels 20 to 37, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the sensors and signals connected to channels 20 to 37 may give wrong values, and a number of supervision alarms may occur simultaneously.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 20 to 37. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F13 failure
alarms.long_description:
Fuse 13 is blown. Fuse 13 protects the power outlets of:
channels 40 to 47, terminal 'D', 
channels 48 to 53, terminal 'E',
channels 60 and 61, terminal 'H'.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: A number of the signals related to channels 40 to 61 may be wrong. Effect on engine behaviour is unknown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for possible failures in the external cabling to channels 40 to 61. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F14 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 14 is blown. Fuse 14 protects the power supply for the analog output, channels 70 and 71, of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: Unable to control VT and Bypass valves.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to channels 70 and 71. Replace the fuse. If the fuse blows again: Replaced the MPC.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->24V power supervision->Fuse F9 failure
alarms.long_description: Fuse 9 is blown. Fuse 9 protects power supply connector 9 of the MPC.
alarms.cause: Electrical overload or wear of the fuse.
alarms.effect: No effect.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for failures in the external cabling to connector 9. Replace the fuse.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->System->Battery Level Low
alarms.long_description: MPC battery level low.
alarms.cause: Battery discharged.
alarms.effect: If MPC remains switched on, there is no effect. If the MPC is switched off or power is lost, the MPC will loose its time settings. Time settings will be automatically retrieved at next power on.
alarms.suggested_action:
At next engine stop:
 1) Remove power supply on MPC.
 2) Replace battery.
 3) Reconnect power supply.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->ECS Commands->No Commands Received from EICU
alarms.long_description: No control values received from EICU
alarms.cause: - EICU failure, or\n- Network failure
alarms.effect: SCU does not receive a set point. Last valid value will be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch to manual scavenging air pressure control

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->ECS Commands->No Commands Received from EICU
alarms.long_description: No control values received from EICU
alarms.cause: - EICU failure, or\n- Network failure
alarms.effect: SCU does not receive a set point. Last valid value will be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch to manual scavenging air pressure control

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Slow Down Request (TC Overspeed)
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger speed is too high
alarms.cause: - Variable turbocharger/ bypass valve is closed AND current engine load is high, or\n- Measurement equipment failure
alarms.effect: Slowdown request is issued to the safety system.
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Keep engine load below 75%
2. Reset slowdown
3. Set the variable turbocharger/bypass valve to fully open (MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenge Air and select Manual control, requires chief level)
4. Resume normal engine operation.

If the problem persists, check actual variable turbocharger/bypass valve position

If the problem persists, open variable turbocharger/bypass valve by local control or mechanically (refer to actuator manual).

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Slow Down Request (high Pscav)
alarms.long_description: Scavenging air pressure (Pscav) is too high
alarms.cause: - Variable turbocharger/ bypass valve is closed AND current engine load is high, or\n- Measurement equipment failure
alarms.effect: Slowdown request is issued to the safety system.
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Keep engine load below 75%
2. Reset slowdown
3. Set the variable turbocharger/bypass valve to fully open (MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenge Air and select Manual control, requires chief level)
4. Resume normal engine operation.

If the problem persists, check:
- Pscav measurement equipment. Compare to other Pscav measurements. 
- Mechanical position of variable turbocharger/bypass valve

If the problem persists:
Open variable turbocharger/bypass valve by local control or mechanically (refer to actuator manual).

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch21,8721,Variable EGB Pos. FB->Suprv. Ch21,8721,Variable EGB Pos.
alarms.long_description: Pscav sensor is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cabling failure\n- Sensor/actuator failure
alarms.effect: Bypass valve moves to failsafe position
alarms.suggested_action:
Switch to manual bypass valve position control until the problem is solved.

Check:
 - Cabling
 - Position measurement.

NOTE
If engine load above 75% is required, move bypass valve to fully open position

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch37,3035,ECS Insulation (kOhm)->Suprv. Ch37,3035,ECS Insulation (kO
alarms.long_description: Sensor signal is out of range
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or
- Sensor failurer, or missing sensor power supply, or
- MPC input failure, or
- For On/Off type sensors the cause can be a missing or wrong supervision resistor (typically 6.8 kOhm).
alarms.effect: Supervision failure for the insulation detection unit will stop all insulation detection.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide 'test for earth failure in ECS system' for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch34,8784-1,VT1 Pos. FB (Ext. Forma->Suprv. Ch34,8784-1,VT1 Pos. FB (Ext
alarms.long_description: Variable turbocharger position signal is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: Variable turbocharger will use last valid value.
alarms.suggested_action:
Switch to manual variable turbocharger position control until the problem is solved.

Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor

NOTE
If engine load above 75% is required, move variable turbocharger to fully open position

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch22,8784-2,VT2 Pos. FB (Ext. Forma->Suprv. Ch22,8784-2,VT2 Pos. FB (Ext
alarms.long_description: Variable turbocharger position signal is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: Variable turbocharger will use last valid value.
alarms.suggested_action:
Switch to manual variable turbocharger position control until the problem is solved.

Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor

NOTE
If engine load above 75% is required, move variable turbocharger to fully open position

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch35,8801-1,TC1 Speed->Suprv. Ch35,8801-1,TC1 Speed
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger speed signal is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: No turbocharger speed supervision
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor

Redundancy reduced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch23,8801-2,TC2 Speed->Suprv. Ch23,8801-2,TC2 Speed
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger speed signal is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: No turbocharger speed supervision
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor

Redundancy reduced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch26,8772,Incr. Exh. Energy (WHR)->Suprv. Ch26,8772,Incr. Exh. Energy
alarms.long_description: Increase Exhaust energy signal is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: Increase Exhaust energy function will not work -> reference Pscav curve will be used (max Pscav)
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- WHR System Condition and output channel.\n- Cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch27,8773,PT Valve Actual Pos(WHR2)->Suprv. Ch27,8773,PT Valve Actual Po
alarms.long_description: Position feedback signal from Power Turbine Control Valve is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: 'Available Energy' signal to Power Turbine is set to zero, meaning that Power Turbine should not be operated.
alarms.suggested_action: Check cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch24,8612,TC Compressor Inlet Temp.->Suprv. Ch24,8612,TC Compressor Inle
alarms.long_description: TC Compressor Inlet Temperature signal is out of range (4-20mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: Ambient compensation of TC PTO power will not work. System will use ISO default values.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Cabling\n- Sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->IO Terminals->Ch27,8760,TC PTO Power FB->Suprv. Ch27,8760,TC PTO Power FB
alarms.long_description: TC PTO Actual Power signal is out of range (4-20 mA)
alarms.cause: - Cable failure, or\n- TC PTO System Failure
alarms.effect: The TC PTO system will shut down since they will receive a setpoint equal to zero .
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Cabling\n- Check TC PTO System

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Scavenge Air Running Modes->Invalid Running Mode Requested
alarms.long_description: Invalid Running Mode Requested
alarms.cause: The Scavenge Air Running Mode parameters for the selected Running Mode are not marked as being valid.
alarms.effect: Using Scavenge Air Running Mode 1 parameters
alarms.suggested_action: Make sure that all Scavenge Air Running Mode parameters to be used are correct and marked as valid.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Scavenge Air Controller->Automatic control not possible
alarms.long_description: No automatic scavenge air control
alarms.cause: - No connection to engine control system (ECS), or \n- Scavenging air pressure measurement failure, or \n- Load estimation failure.
alarms.effect: No automatic scavenge air control. \nSwitch to manual control, MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Network connection to SCU on MOP: Maintenance -> Network Status\n- Scavenging air pressure cabling, signal must be within range (4-20mA)

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->On/Off Bypass->On/Off Bypass Control Failure
alarms.long_description: On/off bypass valve position control failure
alarms.cause: - On/off bypass valve is stuck, or\n- End stop switch failure
alarms.effect: If only feedback is damaged, the valve will continue to function. Else the valve will have no or limited movement, and be in an undefined position.
alarms.suggested_action:
If on/off bypass valve is stuck: 
Keep engine load below 75% until the problem is solved or it is verified that the valve is in the correct position.

Check:
- Actuator cabling
- If bypass valve can move
- Actuator end stop switches

alarms.synopsis: No Air for On/Off Bypass Actuator
alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->On/Off Bypass->No Air for On/Off Bypass Actuator
alarms.long_description: Insufficient control air pressure to actuate on/off exhaust gas bypass
alarms.cause: - Control air pressure is being vented, or \n- Air control system failure
alarms.effect: On/off bypass valve is forced open
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Air pressure sensors\n- Control air system

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->VTI (Variable Turbine Inlet) Valve->VTI Valve Control Failure
alarms.long_description: Variable Turbine Inlet (VTI) Valve position control failure
alarms.cause: - VTI Valve is stuck, or\n- End stop switch failure
alarms.effect: If only feedback is damaged, the valve will continue to function. Else the valve will have no or limited movement, and be in an undefined position.
alarms.suggested_action:
If VTI Valve is stuck: Keep Engine Load below 75% until the problem is solved or it is verified that the
valve is in the correct position
Check:
- Actuator cabling
- If VTI Valve can move
- Actuator end stop switches

alarms.synopsis: No Air for VTI Valve Actuator
alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->VTI (Variable Turbine Inlet) Valve->No Air for VTI Valve Actuator
alarms.long_description: Insufficient control air pressure to actuate Variable Turbine Inlet (VTI) Valve
alarms.cause: - Control air pressure is being vented, or \n- Air control system failure
alarms.effect: VTI Valve is forced open.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Air pressure sensors\n- Control air system

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Var. Valve Overspeed Handling->TC Overspeed
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger speed is too high
alarms.cause: - Bypass valve is too open for the current engine load, or\n- Measurement equipment failure, or\n- Mechanical turbocharger failure
alarms.effect: Bypass valve automatically attempts to open fully to reduce the turbocharger speed. \nIf this attempt reduces the speed sufficiently, the alarm is cancelled, bypass valve control will switch back to normal control.
alarms.suggested_action: Reduce engine load to below 75%\n\nIf engine load above 75% is required, open bypass valve mechanically or via MOP.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Var. EGB Manual Control->Local Control (service term.)
alarms.long_description: MPC Service Terminal controls bypass valve (local control)
alarms.cause: User has enabled service terminal control
alarms.effect: No automatic bypass valve control.\nNo MOP control.
alarms.suggested_action: Disable service terminal control as soon as service terminal operation is completed.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Var. EGB Manual Control->Var. EGB Manual Bypass Control
alarms.long_description: Main Operating Panel (MOP) controls the bypass valve
alarms.cause: Manual control has been activated on MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air screen.
alarms.effect: No automatic scavenging air pressure control
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic mode when manual operation is completed: Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air (Chief level access required)

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Var. EGB Setpoint Deviation->Position deviation (Reset Required)
alarms.long_description: Bypass valve position deviates from the set point
alarms.cause:
- Bypass valve stiction, or
- Bypass actuator failure, or
- Cable failure, or
- MPC failure
alarms.effect:
No bypass valve control.  
Last valid bypass valve position set point is used.

NOTE
If bypass valve is stuck in closed or partly closed position, keep the engine load below 75%
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Reset bypass valve control on MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air -> Variable bypass (requires chief level and manual control)
2. Reset actuator on MOP
3. Power bypass valve off and on.

If the problem persists:
- Check cabling and mechanics
- Recalibrate bypass valve

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Trip And Shutdown Handler->PT/TCPTO Trip Handling Active
alarms.long_description: WHR power turbine or TC PTO system trip signal has been activated
alarms.cause: Internal trip in Power turbine or TC PTO system or generator or cable failure.
alarms.effect: Exhaust bypass is opened instantaneously, to avoid high T/C speed. Normal control after 5- 30\nseconds.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- WHR/TC PTO system/PMS system.
If alarm continues with no indication on PMS/WHR/TC PTO system system:
- Check Cabling.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Trip And Shutdown Handler->Engine Shutdown Handling Active
alarms.long_description: Engine Shutdown Handling Active
alarms.cause: Consult other alarms
alarms.effect: Exhaust bypass is opened and then ramped to closed position. Normal control after 5- 30 seconds
alarms.suggested_action: Consult other alarms

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Bypass Manual
alarms.long_description: Bypass valve control has switched to manual
alarms.cause: User has switched to manual control on MOP
alarms.effect: No automatic bypass valve position control
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->VTI Valve Manual
alarms.long_description: Variable Turbine Inlet (VTI) Valve control has switched to manual
alarms.cause: Manual control has been activated on the MOP screen\n(MOP -> Auxiliaries -> Scavenge Air -> VTI Valve Mode -> Manual)
alarms.effect: No automatic VTI Valve position control.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed\n(MOP -> Auxiliaries -> Scavenge Air -> VTI Valve Mode -> Automatic). Chief Level access is required.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Variable Bypass Command Failed
alarms.long_description: No valid bypass valve set point
alarms.cause: - No connection to engine control system (ECS), or \n- Scavenging air pressure measurement failure, or \n- Load estimation failure.
alarms.effect: No automatic scavenge air control. \nSwitch to manual control, MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Network connection to SCU on MOP: Maintenance -> Network Status\n- Scavenging air pressure cabling, signal must be within range (4-20mA)

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Exercise Function Activated
alarms.long_description: Exercise Function is activated.
alarms.cause: The valve is activated with certain intervals according to parameters.
alarms.effect: Exhaust Gas Bypass is briefly moved away from its setpoint in order to avoid getting stucked.
alarms.suggested_action: The behavior is normal.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT Common Functions->Manual Control->Local Control (service term.)
alarms.long_description: MPC Service Terminal controls variable turbocharger (Local control)
alarms.cause: User has enabled service terminal control
alarms.effect: No automatic variable turbocharger control.\nNo MOP control.
alarms.suggested_action: Disable service terminal control as soon as service terminal operation is completed.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT Common Functions->Manual Control->Manual VT Control
alarms.long_description: Main Operating Panel (MOP) controls the variable turbocharger
alarms.cause: Manual control has been activated on MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air screen.
alarms.effect: No automatic scavenging air pressure control
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control when manual operation is completed. Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air (Chief level access required)

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT1 Supervision->Setpoint Deviation->Position deviation (Reset Required)
alarms.long_description: Variable turbocharger position deviates from the set point
alarms.cause:
- Mechanical failure, or
- Actuator calibration failure, or
- Electrical failure, or
- Actuator failure, or
- Cable failure
alarms.effect:
No variable turbocharger control.  
Last valid variable turbocharger set point is used. 

NOTE
If variable turbocharger is stuck in closed or partly closed position, keep the engine load below 75%
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Reset variable turbocharger control on MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenging Air -> TC  (requires chief level and manual control) 
2. Reset actuator on MOP 
3. Power variable turbocharger cabinet off and on.

If the problem persists:
Check cabling and mechanics.
Recalibrate variable turbocharger

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT1 Supervision->Overspeed Handling->TC Overspeed
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger speed is too high
alarms.cause: - Variable turbocharger is closed AND current engine load is high, or\n- Measurement equipment failure, or\n- Mechanical turbocharger failure
alarms.effect: Variable turbocharger automatically attempts to open fully to reduce the turbocharger speed. \nIf this reduces the speed sufficiently, the alarm is cancelled, and variable turbocharger control will switch back to normal control.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce engine load to below 75%

NOTE
If engine load above 75% is required, move variable turbocharger to fully open position

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT1 Supervision->Torque Limits->VT actuator torque high
alarms.long_description: Actuator torque is too high
alarms.cause: - Mechanical failure, or\n- Actuator failure, or\n- Insufficient variable turbocharger actuator scaling
alarms.effect: SCU attempts full variable turbocharger opening (failsafe position)
alarms.suggested_action: Reset unit\nCheck variable turbocharger

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT1 Supervision->Torque Limits->VT actuator torque high high
alarms.long_description: Actuator torque is too high
alarms.cause: - Mechanical failure, or\n- Actuator failure, or\n- Insufficient variable turbocharger actuator scaling
alarms.effect: SCU attempts full variable turbocharger opening (failsafe position)
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Variable turbocharger 
- Actuator temperature 

If the problem persist and continued operation is necessary: 
Reset actuator on MOP: Auxiliaries -> Scavenge Air or power off/on variable turbocharge.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT1 Supervision->Actuator Failure Handling->Actuator Reports Fault
alarms.long_description: Variable turbocharger is not ready
alarms.cause:
- No power on actuator/control cabinet, or
- Control cabinet fuse is blown, or
- Cable failure (MPC ch. 40), or
- Actuator failure, or 
- Torque too high
alarms.effect: Variable turbocharger does not move.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the variable turbocharger is closed or partially closed, keep engine load below 75%. If engine load above 75% is required, move variable turbocharger to fully open position.

Reset actuator (on MOP or power variable turbocharger off and on).

If the problem persists, check:
- Cabling
- Actuator power
- Variable turbocharger

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Variable Turbocharging->VT2 Supervision->Setpoint Deviation->Position deviation (Reset Required)
alarms.long_description: Variable turbocharger position deviates from the set point
alarms.cause:
- Mechanical failure, or
- Actuator calibration failure, or
- Electrical failure, or
- Actuator failure, or
- Cable failure
alarms.effect:
No variable turbocharger control.

alarms.synopsis: PT Flow Area Above Max Allowed
alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Waste Heat Recovery 2->PT Flow Area Above Max Allowed
alarms.long_description: Power Turbine control valve exceeds the Allowed Level for too long time.
alarms.cause:
Power Turbine has not reduced opening of the control valve to allowed level.
Signals -allowed and actual Power Turbine have wrong values.

The signal 'PT Valve Actual Position' signal  has a value above the signal  'Available Exh. Energy'
alarms.effect: Low scavenging air pressure - leading to low efficiency.\nHigh exhaust and combustion chamber temperatures leading to increased wear on components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- WHR/PMS system.
- signal levels on WHR and ECS systems.
Reduce Power Turbine control valve opening if possible.
If Power turbine control valve continues to operate significantly above allowed level, Power Turbine should be disabled in the load ranges where it operates above limit

alarms.synopsis: TC PTO Power Above Max Allowed
alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Waste Heat Recovery 2->TC PTO Power Above Max Allowed
alarms.long_description: TC PTO power has exceeded the Allowed Level for too long time.
alarms.cause:
TC PTO system has not reduced power take out to allowed level.
Signals -Max Allowed and Actual TC PTO power have incorrect values.

The signal ' TC PTO Actual Power' has a value above the signal 'TC PTO, Max Allowed Power'
alarms.effect: Low scavenging air pressure - leading to low efficiency.\nHigh exhaust and combustion chamber temperatures leading to increased thermal stress on engine\ncomponents.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- TC PTO system/PMS system.
- Signal levels on TC PTO and ECS systems.

Reduce TC PTO power if possible.
If TC PTO system continues to operate significantly above allowed level, TC PTO system should be
disabled in the load ranges where it operates above limit
